The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) 'DoD Implementation Plan from the Commission on Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) Reform Final Report', to facilitate the effort to rapidly increase Navy Lethality in the Submarine and This Budget Line Item (BLI) consists of three separate and distinct programs, the OPNAV N98 sponsored Aircraft Carrier Tactical Support Center (CV-TSC) program, the OPNAV N96 sponsored Sonar Dome Rubber Windows (SDRW) program, and the OPNAV N2N6 sponsored Undersea Warfare Decision Support System (USW-DSS) program. AIRCRAFT CARRIER TACTICAL SUPPORT CENTER (CV-TSC) (Cost Code VM301): The AN/SQQ-34 Aircraft Carrier Tactical Support Center (CV-TSC) program delivers Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) and Surface Warfare (SUW) combat capability to the Aircraft Carrier supporting Aircraft Carrier, Nuclear power (CVN) Tactical Action Office (TAO) and embarked Carrier Strike Group (CSG) Sea Combat Commander. The program provides validation and certification of Engineering Changes (ECs) fielded on CVNs and provides hardware/software changes/upgrades to previously fielded and in-production CV-TSC systems required to correct deficiencies identified through Fleet use, upgrade unreliable/ unsupportable components, replace obsolete components, and resolve Information Assurance (IA) issues. The program maintains interoperability with current and future interfaces to stay within the current performance envelope, supports mission data exchange, improves ASW/SUW track/sensor processing and analysis techniques, improves mission planning, improves data recording, reconstruction, and distribution, improves embedded simulation and training capabilities and implements cyber-security measures to effectively employ overall CVN Self Ship Defense System (SSDS) capabilities. CV-TSC integrates sensor data from organic Aircraft (MH-60R), organic platform sensors and tracks via Ship Self Defense System Product Line Architecture (PLA) and non-PLA, Link-16 track data, Global Command and Control System (GCCS) Over-the-Horizon track data, and Environmental and Threat Databases to assess the threat and assist the Tactical Action Officer and Carrier Strike Group to effectively employ overall CVN self- defense capabilities. CV-TSC generates real-time ASW/SUW information and recommendations, tactical planning and employment of ASW/SUW assets, ASW/SUW sensor data processing and analysis, and distribution of tactically significant data. Aircraft supported include: MH-60R/S Seahawk, P-8 Poseidon, MQ-4C Triton, and future ASW/SUW non-organic supporting platforms. SONAR DOME RUBBER WINDOWS (SDRWs) (Cost Code VM401): AN/SQS-53 Sonar Dome Rubber Windows (SDRWs) are installed on all CG47 and DDG51 class ships (Initial Capabilities Document (ICD) for ASW, AN/SQQ-89(V) Operational Requirements Document (ORD) (#667-76-05 dated August 2005). This program provides emergency replacement, wire-reinforced, pressurized rubber acoustic windows and attachment hardware, which experience failure due to corrosion, fatigue, and impact damage. Ships with a severely damaged SDRW need to be dry-docked, so continually monitoring status of SDRWs and maintaining a ready inventory of replacement assets is a priority in order to keep ships on mission. The SDRW significantly improves the surface ship sonar performance by reducing flow-induced self-noise and by providing increased source level receiving and sensitivity resulting from reduced attenuation. This program provides production engineering in support of technical evaluations, failure analysis, implementation of the in-water one-side backscatter X-ray program, Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) refurbishments of production systems and field service engineering; and completion of engineering design work and material tests. This program also provides drawings, configuration management information, incorporation of new design and fabrication technology, incorporation of lessons learned and required testing, and constructs sub-elements to confirm single-stage cure of UNDERSEA WARFARE DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEM (USW-DSS) (Cost Code VM601): USW-DSS is the Navy Program of Record ASW Command and Control (C2) Net-Centric system supporting the warfighter. USW-DSS provides an integrated, near-real time, net-centric ASW Common Tactical Picture (CTP) and Common Operational Picture (COP) for the Carrier Strike Groups (CSGs). USW-DSS is a C2 capability identified in the ASW Initial Capabilities Document (ICD), for the Sea Combat Commander (SCC) and Theater USW Commander (TUSWC). USW-DSS enables effective planning and execution of Undersea Warfare (USW) operations, optimizes placement of sensors for exploitation of the environment, manages available resources, balances operations versus risk, and provides a clear vulnerability assessment of the operational environment. USW-DSS shortens C2 decision processes for detection-to-engagement across multiple platforms, including those with low bandwidth communications or intermittent connectivity. Tactical data such as tracks, environmental, and sensor processing data is ingested into USW-DSS through platform specific interfaces such as the AN/SQQ-89(V) Surface Ship ASW Combat System, the Global Command and Control System - Maritime (GCCS-M), and Aircraft Carrier Tactical Support Center (CV-TSC). USW-DSS processes this and other tactical data and supports intelligent dissemination of the data to unit level and theater level platforms in support of an enhanced USW tactical picture. USW-DSS provides USW Commanders with an expanded, net-centric USW collaborative capability across CSG platforms (CVNs, CGs, DDGs) as well as supporting shore nodes to include: Theater Undersea Warfare Command Headquarters (TUSWCHQ), the Naval Oceanographi 2176 2027 Undersea Warfare Support Equipment 1810N BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip

events.text: 1810N line 2210 Submarine Acoustic Warfare System: FY2026 $56.482M, FY2027 $68.881M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 3 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2210 / Submarine Acoustic Warfare System (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) The Submarine Acoustic Warfare System (SAWS) program provides submarines with expendable defensive countermeasures and the systems necessary to launch them against torpedo and acoustic sensor threats. This program provides ongoing production of countermeasure devices needed to sustain fleet inventories, improvements to enhance the readiness and effectiveness of countermeasure devices and associated External Countermeasure Launcher (ECL) systems on all U.S. submarines. Acoustic Device Countermeasures (ADC) are expendable devices produced in two primary versions. The Internal Countermeasure Launcher (ICL) launches the 3" ADCs and ECL Systems launch the 6" devices. WM014 6 Inch Countermeasures: Funding under this cost code procures and supports 6" Countermeasures, ADC MK3 (torpedo), and ADC MK4 (SONAR) countermeasures for submarine protection. The effort includes unit costs of the new devices, reworks, and the system engineering, which covers the associated support costs at the Technical Design Agent (TDA) and In-Service Engineering Activity (ISEA). For every procurement of 6-inch ADC, supplementary MK77 shall be procured. WM015 3 Inch Countermeasures: Funding under this cost code procures and supports 3" Countermeasures ADC MK2 for submarine protection. This effort includes the unit costs of the devices as well as the system engineering services, which covers the associated support costs at the TDA and ISEA. The effort also includes procurement of an enhanced ADC MK2 MOD 8/9 that provides the Fleet with greater WM018 Acoustic Augmentation Support Program (AASP): Funding under this cost code provides acoustic augmentation systems in appropriate configurations for all submarine classes (except SEAWOLF). The equipment is installed as temporary equipment Temporary Alteration (TEMPALT) until Ship Alterations (SHIPALTs) can be permanently installed to reduce sustainment costs and provide a long-term solution. A combination of new procurement systems and refurbished systems are required to complete installations. Reliability and refurbishment upgrades provide current in-service AASP systems with new components and software updates to maintain reliability. AASP new procurements are required a year prior to installation and refurbished systems are required the same year as installation. WM019 Countermeasure Set, Acoustic (CSA) Program: Funding under this cost code procures and supports the inboard electronic system necessary for preparing and launching 6" ADCs from all 688i and newer U.S. submarines. This inboard system consists of the Torpedo Defense Controller (TDC), Launch Control Panels (LCPs), and associated cabling, in a class-by-class configuration. The CSA program continually modernizes and technical refreshes system hardware and software. Five efforts are supported: (1) The "CSA SWFTS Integration" effort is maintaining the integration of the CSA system with the SWFTS System of Systems (SoS). Implementation of a phased approach allowed incremental implementation of capabilities. Required funding addresses recurring upgrades within the SWFTS Technology Insertion (TI)/Advanced Processor Build (APB) cycles to maintain compatibility with networked tactical systems and continue to reduce cybersecurity risks. (2) The ongoing "CSA MK4 Technology Insertion" effort replaces the CSA MK2 MOD2 with a SubTDS-capable, SWFTS-integrated CSA MK4 system on VIRGINIA Class Block I and II submarines (10 hulls). (3) The "CSA SEAWOLF SWFTS Integration" effort replaces the CSA MK2 MOD5 system being installed on the SEAWOLF Class submarines (3 hulls) with a SubTDS-capable, SWFTS-integrated CSA system. The non-recurring engineering effort (to develop the SHIPALT drawings that address mounting and cable changes and the software development effort in support of the MK5 system going on the SEAWOLF) began in FY21 with fielding beginning in FY23 as part of the SWFTS TI-22 baseline. (4) The "CSA SWFTS Virtualization" effort supports the development and integration of the CSA system with the AN/BYG-1 Combat Control System on VIRGINIA and COLUMBIA new construction hulls. (5) The fifth effort is the ongoing support for engineering issues across all CSA systems as they arise. WM022 MK77 Gas Generator (GG): Funding under this cost code procures and supports Gas Generators used to launch 6-inch devices from the submarine. The effort includes unit costs of the new devices, reworks, and the system engineering which covers the associated support costs at the TDA and ISEA. Gas Generators are required on a one for one basis with 6-inch devices (ADC MK3, MK4, CRAW and ADC WM025 Compact Rapid Attack Weapon (CRAW): Funding under this cost code procures the required integration kits and other required submarine support equipment for the CRAW MK58 torpedo. The MK58 torpedo provides enhanced Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) and Anti-Torpedo Torpedo (ATT) mission capabilities to the submarine Force. The MK58 torpedo is launched from VIRGINIA Class (VACL) submarines via the integration kits for the ECL and payload control system that are procured from this line item. Note, the MK58 torpedoes will be procured separately via WPN (LI 3121). VB700 Payload Procurement: Funding under this cost code extends the sensor range of the submarine. Procurement of SLUAS AURs include the UAV, launch, canister, and supporting auxiliary equipment. Sustains the in-service system AN/SLQ-25A/C (NIXIE) countermeasure. Modernizes NIXIE to the AN/SLQ-25E variant with a technical and obsolescence refresh that also provides the baseline. The AN/SLQ-25 (NIXIE) is the Navy's primary SSTD system, providing towed persistent torpedo countermeasure. NIXIE currently protects all classes of surface ships. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) PROGRAM COVERAGE: Surveillance Towed Array Sensor System (SURTASS) is the mobile, tactical, and strategic arm of the Navy's undersea surveillance capability that provides deep ocean and littoral acoustic detection and cueing for tactical weapon platforms against diesel and nuclear submarines as well as surface vessels in any given Area of Operations worldwide. Dedicated Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) T-AGOS ships tow long acoustic arrays that collect acoustic data and relay that data to shore facilities via satellites for processing and fusion of the resulting contact data with other sensors. Currently, there are five Small Waterplane Area Twin Hull (SWATH) Passive (P)/Active (A) T-AGOS ships operating in the Pacific area. Ship configurations are: T-AGOS 22 USNS LOYAL (1), a SWATH-P platform which supports passive operations using the TB-29A Twinline (TL-29A) array, providing improved detection and classification capability. This ship class uses the Integrated Common Processor (ICP) signal processing and display system common with the SSN Acoustic Rapid Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) Insertion (ARCI) Sonar Processing System. processing and display system, the TL-29A array, and the Compact Low Frequency Active (CLFA) transmit capability. One (1) Low Frequency Active (LFA) equipped ship, T-AGOS 23 USNS IMPECCABLE, a SWATH-A platform configured with the ICP processing and display system, the TL-29A array, and the Low Frequency Active (LFA) transmit capability. The active capability provides greatly improved detection against diesel submarines as well as the quiet nuclear submarine threat. In addition to the five platforms described above, two (2) shore sites are configured with the ICP processing and display suites to receive the T-AGOS acoustic data via Super High Frequency (SHF) satellite communication links. One of the two shore sites is equipped with three (3) SURTASS Team Trainers (STTs) to support Home Port Training Periods. A cost sharing agreement with Japan also provides two (2) shore sites and four (4) Japanese SWATH ships with similar capability to the T-AGOS SWATH-P ships for the Western Pacific region. Funding supports the U.S. cost share for the procurement of Towed Arrays for the new J-AOS-4 ship. The Expeditionary Surveillance Towed Array Sensor System (SURTASS-E) provides a SURTASS passive capability packaged in ISO-Vans (ISO-International Organization for Standardization) for mobilization on Vessels of Opportunity (VOOs). It was developed as a Rapid Prototyping, Experimentation, and Demonstration (RPED) project, tasked to re-package, test, and demonstrate an expeditionary variant of the passive component of the SURTASS acoustic surveillance system that can be used as a surrogate for some of the SURTASS capabilities provided by traditional T-AGOS class vessels. It was developed as a Rapid Prototyping, Experimentation, and Demonstration (RPED) project, tasked to re-package, test, and demonstrate an expeditionary variant of the passive component of the SURTASS acoustic surveillance system that can be used as a surrogate for some of the SURTASS capabilities provided by traditional T-AGOS class [P40A / SURTASS-E Kits]: The Expeditionary Surveillance Towed Array Sensor System (SURTASS-E) provides a SURTASS passive capability packaged in ISO-Vans (ISO-International Organization for [P40A / Deep Water Active (DWA)]: The Deployable Surveillance Systems (DSS), complementing the Fixed Surveillance System (FSS) and Surveillance Towed Array Sensor System (SURTASS), provides flexible and responsive wide area surveillance to the Theater Undersea Warfare (TUSW) commanders worldwide. DSS will operate as adjunct systems to meet the established FSS and SURTASS missions and to meet additional missions as articulated in the OPNAV Top Level Requirements documents and follow-on Course of Action Analysis (COAA) and as dictated by TUSW commanders evolving and emergent operational requirements. DSS is comprised of the following systems: Deep Water Passive (DWP) and Deep Water Active (DWA). Informed by TUSW Offset operations and the tailored requirements process, the DSS Middle Tier Acquisition (MTA) Rapid Fielding Program focused initially on the DWP increment and associated spiral development updates. Spiral developments to meet the evolving submarine threat will leverage on-going Navy, Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), and small business research efforts including processing and sensor technology. FY27 includes funds for DWA that will provide a rapidly deployable sustained surveillance capability in response to emergent Fleet Undersea Warfare (USW) coverage gaps to include mitigating array outages or platform shortages. events.text: 1810N line 2312 AN/SLQ-32: FY2026 $422.704M, FY2027 $653.483M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 5 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2312 / AN/SLQ-32 (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) AN/SLQ-32: Provides surface combatants defensive and offensive electronic warfare capabilities that are critical to ship-based layered defense. Defensive systems provide Electronic Support (ES) capability- searching for, identifying, and tracking sources of electromagnetic (EM) energy for the purpose of immediate threat recognition, targeting, planning, and conducting of future operations. ES systems complement other ship-based sensors and contribute to a surface combatant's overall picture of its threat environment. Offensive systems provide Electronic Attack (EA) capability- directing EM energy to defeat enemy fires. This non-kinetic soft-kill capability broadens ship self-defense options, deepens magazines, provides reduced logistics, and lowers "cost-per-shot" compared to kinetic munitions. AN/SLQ-32(V) is the core of surface electronic warfare (EW) capability. Navy has fielded surface electronic warfare systems designated as AN/SLQ-32(V)1-7. AN/SLQ-32(V)1-5 are legacy systems no longer in production. AN/SLQ-32(V)6 is an ES system currently in production. AN/SLQ-32(V)7, which builds on (V)6, is also in production, and it provides offensive EA at the strike group level. Scaled Onboard Electronic Attack (SOEA) is a future capability currently in development that will provide EA self-protection capability to ships unable to support AN/SLQ-32(V)7 due to size, weight, power, and cooling. The Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program (SEWIP) provides progressively greater capability through a series of block upgrades to AN/SLQ-32(V) systems: - SEWIP Block 1 provided federated Specific Emitter Identification (SEI), an upgraded console and display, and High-Gain High-Sensitivity (HGHS). (Navy recently divested of these requirements for higher priorities ). to size, weight, power, and cooling constraints. - SEWIP Block 3 provides Electronic Attack (EA) capability. Signal Processing Upgrade was previously referred to as VPX Tech Refresh. Updating the name to better describe full capability being delivered with the upgrade to the below deck equipment. Since the FY26 budget request, (V)6 VPX Upgrade Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) has been renamed AN/SLQ-32(V) Signal Processing Upgrade to more accurately describe full capability being delivered with the upgrade to the below deck equipment. The Signal Processing Upgrade is the below deck computing power behind surface EW capabilities. The Signal Processor upgrade integrates above deck hardware components with each other and the combat system. Signal Processing Upgrades are critical enablers of the added capabilities delivered by SEWIP block upgrades and next-generation countermeasures. Countermeasures are a critical component of surface EW capability and integrate with the combat system and AN/SLQ-32 via the Signal Processing Upgrade. NULKA, Long Endurance Electronic Decoy (LEED), and MK-59 soft-kill threats use EM energy to deceive a threat's guidance system. Countermeasures are funded via Budget Line Item 5530. In FY27, Navy is taking a fresh approach to acquisition of AN/SLQ-32 systems. The program office is breaking from single source contracting and instead implementing an Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity Multiple Award Contract (IDIQ MAC) strategy aimed at lowering costs and broadening the surface EW industrial base. The new contracting approach will open competition for AN/SLQ-32 production contracts by empowering industry partners to bid at the individual task order level. Industry partners will no longer be required to deliver an entire AN/SLQ-32 system. Rather, they will leverage their core competencies by delivering components of an AN/SLQ-32 system. Individual components will be integrated by Navy's organic industrial base. Block 1 + Block 2 + SOEA = Nomenclature TBD SURFACE ELECTRONIC WARFARE (EW) IMPROVEMENTS BLOCK 1: The program will divest High-Gain High-Sensitivity (HGHS Block 1B3) and Specific Emitter Identification (SEI Block 1B2) capabilities. SURFACE ELECTRONIC WARFARE (EW) IMPROVEMENTS BLOCK 2: SEWIP Block 2 provides an upgraded antenna, receiver, and combat systems interface. The upgrades will pace the evolving threat, improve detection and accuracy, and mitigate Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). The Block 2 hardware cost includes the SEWIP Block 2 ES system, Blanker-Video Mixer Group (AN/SLA-10D), Common Processing System, Common Display System, Liquid Conditioning Unit, and Data Adaptation Processor. The SEWIP Block 2, and Block 3 units are installed conjunctively to compose the AN/SLQ-32(V)7 system. AN/SLQ-32(V) Signal Processing Upgrade (previously the (V)6 VPX Upgrade Engineering Change Proposal (ECP)) provides significant capability and reliability enhancements that greatly increase the AN/ SLQ-32(V) operator's tactical situational awareness and system availability. In addition, modernization provides the back-end computing power necessary to counter emerging threats. It increases system emitter processing throughput, reduces false detections/classifications, increases system fault tolerance, simplifies system maintenance, and is a critical enabler of future artificial intelligence (AI) capability growth required to rapidly ID and classify emerging unknown threat emitters. Signal Processing Upgrade is also a pre-requisite for EW systems currently in development, such as LEED and SOEA. SURFACE ELECTRONIC WARFARE (EW) IMPROVEMENTS BLOCK 3: Block 3 provides Electronic Attack (EA) capability improvement required for the AN/SLQ-32(V) system to keep pace with the evolving threat. The program builds on the EW Electronic Support (ES) capability delivered by Block 2 and will provide a common EA capability to surface ships (CVN, DDG, and LHD). The program works in concert with Scaled O 2312 2027 AN/SLQ-32 1810N BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip

Funding for LI 3501 Cryptologic Carry-On Program (CCOP) has been realigned into LI 2360 Shipboard Information Warfare (IW) as part of Other Procurement, Navy Line Item-Consolidation starting in FY 2026. This effort consolidates the existing number of PEs/BLIs identified by BSOs and FMB to group technology projects to allow flexibility that would foster innovation and promote efficiency. PE/BLI consolidation meets the DoW Implementation Plan from the Commission on PPBE Interim Report. The Shipboard Information Warfare (IW) budget supports Ships Signal Exploitation Equipment (SSEE) Increment F, its variants, and Engineering Change Proposals (ECP) to maintain pace with modernization and signal threats; SSEE Modifications (SSEE MODS); Spectral; Integrated Communications and Data System (ICADS) Increments II and III; Real Time Spectrum Operations (RTSO); Horizon; Distributed Operations (DO); Advanced IW Antennas (AIWA); Cryptologic Carry-On-Program (CCOP); Snakehead, and Pacific Fleet Urgent Operational Need (PACFLT UON). The SSEE Family of Systems (FoS) includes variants which introduce scalability and configuration modularity through a permanently installed SSEE systems and Topside Infrastructure (Topside Antennas) supplemented with mission modules to meet platform mission requirements for Over the Horizon Targeting (OTH-T), and Counter-Command, Control, Computing, Communications, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance and Targeting (C- C5ISRT). Mission module and ECP capabilities integrated into the SSEE Systems will enable maritime power projection by providing surface vessels the ability to disrupt, deny, degrade and defeat adversary (state and non-state) use of radio frequency spectrum, improving the Fleet's ability to communicate and operate therein. As part of the National Security Agency's (NSA) "Secure the Network" & "Secure the Enterprise" initiatives, NSA and C10F (10th Fleet) requires all systems, including U.S. Navy Surface Cryptologic Systems to The CCOP procures state-of-the-art, commercial off-the-shelf Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) equipment (hardware and software) in response to combatant commander requirements for a quick-reaction surface cryptologic carry-on capability. The equipment is procured in accordance with requirements detailed in the shipboard Information Warfare / Cryptologic System Operational Requirements Document and specific execution year fleet requirements. These requirements are defined by Fleet Cyber Command (FCC)/Commander TENTH Fleet (C10F) Fleet Signals Development Working Group (FSDWG), in concert with Shipboard Signals Exploitation Space (SSES) programs (includes Ship's Signal Exploitation Equipment Family of Systems) to ensure synergy and seamless transition to permanently installed systems. The FSDWG meets to determine which signals of interest (SOI)s/Targets on the FSDWG list need to be addressed. Due to a continually changing threat environment, detailed requirements are dynamic and equipment procured varies each year by quantity and type. Equipment suites can be configured for many targets and tasking. Target specific subsystems can either operate as stand-alone within the cryptologic spaces or as an add-on to existing equipment. Hardware procurements includes: receivers, recorders, tactical computers and related peripherals, antennas, electronic-warfare support measures systems, precision geolocation equipment, advanced signal and search equipment including spectrum analyzers and associated portable special intelligence communications equipment. CCOP equipment is installed as an augment to cryptologic capabilities on surface units. There are approximately 120 cryptologic capable surface ships and shore sites in the current Navy inventory. Each of these are potential users of this carry-on equipment. The temporary installation of equipment is coordinated through fleet augmentation requests and installed by fleet electronic support personnel. A primary system in inventory is the Carry On Radio Spectrum Analysis & Intelligence Reporting (CORSAIR) system. Funds continue to procure CORSAIR core architecture system upgrades to provide additional affordable functionality to the combatant commands. Additional signal acquisition equipment to address specific combatant command requirements include such systems as PTEK, Digital Receiver Technology (DRT), Hostile forces Integrated Targeting Service (HITS), Maritime Toxic Pen (MTP), TURBULENTWAVE / TURBULENTSAIL / BLUESTREAM servers, RED FALCON, FIREFLY, NIBBLE TRACTOR, SHEARWATER, CARBON STORM, XML to JREAP- C (X2J), TOXIC SMOKE, QUICKSHOT, SHOCKWAVE/WSTL, SHARKNADO, MONARCH/SCEPTRE and SALVAGE. [P5 / 1U029 Information Warfare (IW) Training Equipment]: Information Warfare (IW) training equipment provides operator, unit or multi-unit level training on Ships Signal Exploitation Equipment (SSEE) Increment F (V) 7/8. This equipment enhances initial skills, provides refresher training and increases proficiency of the operator on the system through the generation and replay of operational scenarios by software simulation versus hardware simulation. IW training equipment is updated based on new variants of SSEE systems. Additionally, this line supports the procurement of the Stallion (formerly known as Cryptologic On-Line Trainer) hardware for Shipboard IW team training. Stallion is a web-based/Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) scenario training system that emulates Navy Tactical Signal Intelligence (SIGINT)/Information Operations (IO) system functionality. Stallion is delivered turnkey to the Center for Information Warfare Training (CIWTs). The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) Funding for LI 2900 Maritime Integrated Broadcast Service (MIBS) has been realigned into LI 2361 Automatic Identification System (AIS) as part of Other Procurement, Navy Line Item-Consolidation starting in FY 2026. This effort consolidates the existing number of PEs/BLIs identified by BSOs and FMB to group technology projects to allow flexibility that would foster innovation and promote efficiency. PE/BLI consolidation meets the DoW Implementation Plan from the Commission on PPBE Interim Report. 1U030: AIS is required for safety of navigation for all surface ships and submarines. AIS is a maritime Very High Frequency (VHF) communication system, which allows ships to exchange navigation, ship identification, and cargo information machine-to-machine via VHF transponders. AIS provides vessels with the ability to rapidly identify and track commercial shipping, which significantly increases the Navy's ability to distinguish between normal and suspicious merchant ships headed towards United States and allied ports around the globe. AIS provides critical track data to the Common Operational Picture (COP) on surface ships, AN/BYG-1 Combat System on submarines, Global Command and Control System-Maritime (GCCS-M) on Force Level ships, and Global Command and Control System-Joint (GCCS-J) at Fleet Maritime Operations Centers (MOC). The AIS submarine configuration provides an interface to the AN/BYG-1 Combat System and encrypted AIS capability. This capability dramatically improves the Combatant Commanders' situational awareness and Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) data sharing capabilities in support of regional engagement and tracking efforts against potential maritime terrorism threats. Funds will be used to continue the initial fielding of AIS (V)9 Program of Record systems, their follow-on cyber hardening upgrades, as well as the continuation of surface ship cyber hardening. The AIS submarine variant consists of a combination of government/commercial software, AIS power and navigation subsystem, AIS antenna selector switch, AIS antenna interface unit, AIS data distribution laptop, and AIS terminal data processing unit. The need for AIS systems is especially important for submarines, which have limited maneuverability. The AIS (V)3 and (V)9 Submarine configuration provides situational awareness (to include encrypted AIS message traffic from United States Coast Guard vessels) during time-constrained ascents to communications depth, thereby significantly reducing the risk of a collision. In order to address potential vulnerabilities identified by the Naval Cyber Warfare Development Group (NCWDG) and in compliance with the "Expression of Cyber Requirement for Automatic Identification System" dated 31 Jan 2017, a cybersecurity engineering change will be implemented on all AIS systems in order to protect downstream systems from malformed or anomalous AIS data. Funds are being used to procure and install a new Warship AIS compliant transponder and AIS Terminal Box on all AIS (V)1 equipped surface ships. A new small form factor AIS workstation will be procured and installed on Force- Level ships equipped with AIS (V)2 systems. This has already been installed at Fleet HQ MOCs equipped with AIS (V)5 systems. New AIS laptops and Warship AIS compatible transponders will be procured and installed on all submarines equipped with an AIS (V)3 or AIS (V)9 Program of Record system. The above hardware configuration changes are required to implement software and firmware modifications that will detect, log, and filter all incoming AIS data from unverified sources, alert operators to the presence of anomalous AIS data and protect systems and users of AIS data downstream from the data collection point. These users include GCCS-M, GCCS-J, Distributed Common Ground System - Navy (DCGS-N), Electronic Chart Display and Information System - Navy (ECDIS-N), BYG-1, and others. DH530: The MIBS program delivers Integrated Broadcast Service (IBS) data to operational and tactical decision makers aboard United States Navy surface ships, shore headquarters, and other joint platforms. MIBS provides the Navy with the capability to receive and deliver near real time, Over the Air (OTA) IBS data, enhancing the Common Operation Picture (COP) supporting operations in all warfare areas, including Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD), Anti-Air Warfare (AAW), Anti-Surface Warfare (ASUW), Undersea Warfare (UW), Electronic Warfare (EW) and track location of red and blue forces to warfighters at the tactical edge, regardless of Emission Control (EMCON) posture. MIBS provides essential support to the Over the Horizon-Targeting (OTH-T) mission and supports closure of the kill chain in a denied This budget will provide a technical refresh of the Joint Tactical Terminal - Maritime (JTT-M) systems. The Joint Tactical Terminal - Maritime Evolved (JTT-ME) system replaces an End of Life (EoL) JTT- Senior terminals and infrastructure with a modern, secure, network enabled infrastructure that allows flexibility for future radios/waveforms. This system is formally specified by Fleet Commanders as a threshold capability for global Maritime Command, Control and Communications in a Distributed Maritime Environment to execute current Warfighting plans and is required for National Command and Control capability. events.text: 1810N line 2606 Cooperative Engagement Capability: FY2026 $26.648M, FY2027 $33.932M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 4 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2606 / Cooperative Engagement Capability (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) Cooperative Engagement Capability (CEC) significantly improves Battle Force Anti-Air Warfare (AAW) capability by coordinating all Battle Force AAW sensors into a single, real-time, composite track picture capable of fire control quality. CEC distributes sensor data from each ship and aircraft, or cooperating unit (CU), to all other CUs in the battle force through a real-time, line of sight, high data rate sensor and engagement data distribution network. CEC is highly resistant to jamming and provides accurate gridlocking between CUs. Each CU independently employs high capacity, parallel processing and advanced algorithms to combine all distributed sensor data into a fire control quality track picture which is the same for all CUs. CEC data is presented as a superset of the best AAW sensor capabilities from each CU; all of which are integrated into a single input to each CU's combat weapons system. CEC significantly improves Battle Force defense in depth, including both local area and ship defense capabilities against current and future AAW threats. Moreover, CEC provides critical connectivity and integration of over-land air defense systems capable of countering emerging air threats, including land attack cruise missiles, in CEC consists of the Data Distribution System (DDS), the Cooperative Engagement Processor (CEP), and Combat System modifications. The DDS encodes and distributes ownship sensor and engagement data and is a high capacity, jam resistant, directive system providing a precision gridlocking and high throughput of data. The CEP is a high capacity distributed processor that is able to process force levels of data in near real time. This data is passed to the ship's combat system as high quality data for which the ship can cue its onboard sensors or use the data to engage targets without actually tracking them. The CEC suite contains a C-Band antenna, the antenna's power and cooling equipment, a Signal Data Processor (SDP), and system support equipment. The current CEC Shipboard antenna variants include the Shipboard Active Aperture (SBAA) and the Planar Array Antenna Assembly (PAAA). The SDP hosts the CEP software and is common across all CEC variants. The USG-2B articles in this budget procure support hardware consisting of a ruggedized 19-inch rack that contains a Cesium time standard, input/output converter, power distribution and user interface control devices. The 19-inch rack holds the SDP. SBAA and PAAA support are provided by an Antenna Environmental Control Unit (AECU) or Environmental Control System Controller (ECSC), which provide power and cooling oil to the CEC shipboard antenna. Funding provided also procures the required Weapon Replaceable Assembly (WRA) hardware required for airborne variants of CEC. CEC is planned for shipboard installations at various Naval and commercial shipyards aboard CG/CG Mod, DDG/DDG Mod, CV/CVN, LPD, LHD, DDG 1000, and LHA ship classes during scheduled ship availability periods and at land based test sites (LBTS). NTCSS provides organizational maintenance management capabilities for all afloat and ashore operational forces (ships, submarines, expeditionary, and cyber), as well as organizational and intermediate maintenance management to maintain operational availability of deployed and deployable aircraft. NTCSS also provides personnel administration capabilities, planning and execution of warehouse and inventory management functions for repair parts and consumable material, financial accountability thereof, and support services of food and afloat retail point-of-sale operations. NTCSS system upgrades procures afloat and ashore ruggedized, commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) computing equipment, which includes servers to support the NTCSS application and database, personal computers (PCs) that will interface with the servers for maintenance and supply transactions, and printers to display output. The NOBLE family of systems will provide direct support to warfighter readiness with maintenance, supply, and personnel administration capabilities using an open architecture framework that incorporates business process re-engineering (BPR) allowing for the consolidation of standalone application systems. These capabilities include enterprise-wide automation of supply, inventory, and financial functions to the Naval supply system, aviation maintenance support capability that services aviation maintenance (organizational and intermediate) for over 2,100 Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, standardized operational business processes for afloat maritime maintenance activities to all naval ships, expeditionary forces and Navy-wide personnel and administration data sharing across shipboard and shore-based information systems. NOBLE will meet current and emerging demands for cyber, Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR), and Navy logistics and aviation and maritime maintenance Naval Operational Supply System (NOSS) will deliver a solution with enterprise and field level capability to ensure effective and efficient supply operations. NOSS will enable the planning, procurement and physical/financial accountability of all material and property across all warfare communities. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) Advanced Tactical Data Link Systems (ATDLS) is the United States (US) Navy's only ship-to-ship/ship-to-aircraft tactical information solution equipping warfighters and Combatant Commanders with real-time battlespace data and extending the range of lethality. ATDLS is the backbone of Carrier Strike Group and AEGIS-Based Defense operations and is the key component in the fire control loop, providing critical track information for enabling maritime offense/defense, Joint Area Domain Command and Control (JADC2), Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD), Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD), Anti-Air Warfare (AAW), Anti-Surface Warfare (ASuW), Electronic Warfare (EW), Advanced Offboard Electronic Warfare (AOEW), and Long Range Fires (LRF) missions. ATDLS Integration Program develops new and improved Tactical Data Links (TDL) networking capabilities, delivering operational and targeting support to the warfighter. ATDLS rapidly and securely connects carrier/shipboard digital combat systems to military aircraft, ground troops, coalition partners, and space assets with vital Situational Awareness, targeting, and sensor information. ATDLS also provides Joint Range Extension capability via Link 16 Network (Link 16) Terminals, Command and Control Processor (C2P), and Link Monitoring and Management Tool (LMMT). C2P Technology Refresh (TR) and C2P Modernization (MOD) Full Systems Ship/Shore (DR003): C2P is the only shipboard solution that enables bi-directional exchange of tactical information across multiple TDLs within the joint operations areas. C2P processes and exchanges Link 11, Link 16, Satellite TDL J, and Joint Range Extension Applications Protocol (JREAP) tactical data among the US, North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), and allied nation military platforms enabling the vital joint TDL interface. Additionally, C2P provides data translation services, acts as a single interface between host combat system and TDL networks, and forwards tactical data between platforms operating at extended ranges. C2P enables surface platforms capability to conduct Ballistic Missile Defense BMD Launch-on-Remote/Engage- on-Remote and Autonomous Vehicle missions. C2P TR with C2P v3.13 software baseline enables Tactical Targeting Network Technology (TTNT), equipping warfighters with faster network speed and improved capacity. C2P MOD procurements seamlessly cut-in starting FY26 utilizing existing contract strategy. C2P Mod delivers Link 22 capability allowing interoperability with coalition partners; as well as enabling an agile DevSecOps software deployment for rapid capability and cybersecurity upgrades, enabling continuous kill chain improvements. Link 16 TTNT Upgrade Kits (DR012): Link 16 enhanced by TTNT serves as the military's only joint network capable of providing secure tactical data link interoperability and data sharing in contested battlespace environments. These upgrade kits modernize currently fielded Link 16 cabinets through two primary configurations: the Multifunctional Information Distribution System (MIDS) on-Ship (MOS) and MOS Modernization (MOS Mod). The Link 16 TTNT MOS-J Upgrade Kit and Link 16 TTNT MOS Mod enhance existing configurations in accordance with Joint Chiefs of Staff Joint Requirements Oversight Council Memorandum (JROCM) 075-17, enabling the integration and installation of MIDS Joint Tactical Radio System (MIDS JTRS) terminals within Navy shipboard environments. Upgrades in MIDS-JTRS AV6, TTNT power amplifier, external GPS input, and updated controller interface computer. Starting in FY2027, Joint Automated Deep Operations Coordination System (JADOCS) will no longer be funded with OPN and all JADOCS P5a Cost Elements have been removed. JADOCS will continue support of sustainment activities under OMN Program Element 0204660N / Subhead 1C1C / Project Unit 70100. Funding starting in FY2027 includes Global Command and Control System-Maritime (GCCS-M) and the Navy fielded portions of GCCS-Joint (GCCS-J). Prior to FY2027, includes Global Command and Control System-Maritime (GCCS-M), the Navy fielded portions of GCCS-Joint. GCCS-M is the Maritime implementation of the United States (U.S.) Global Command and Control System (GCCS). It provides Maritime Commanders at all echelons of command with a single, integrated, and scalable Command, Control, Communication, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) system that fuses, correlates, filters, maintains and displays location and attributes information on friendly, hostile, and neutral land, sea, and air forces. It takes this information and integrates it with available intelligence and environmental information to support commander decision making. It operates in near real-time, constantly updating unit positions and other situational awareness data. GCCS-M also records data in appropriate databases and maintains a history of changes to those records. System operators use the data to construct relevant tactical pictures using maps, charts, topography overlays, oceanographic overlays, meteorological overlays, imagery and all-source intelligence information coordinated into a Common Operational Picture (COP) that can be shared locally and with other sites. GCCS-M v4.1.5.X provides track management for battle management aids (BMAs) critical to "Fight Tonight". Continuous delivery of GCCS-M v4.1.5 and associated training is required to support the Fleet increased demand for deployment of Carrier Strike Groups. GCCS-M is not a weapon system, but receives data from, and interfaces with Navy integrated weapons systems. Navy Commanders review and evaluate the general tactical situation, plan actions and operations, direct forces, synchronize tactical movements, and integrate force maneuver with firepower. GCCS-M operates on General Service (GENSER) Secret networks in a variety of environments and supports joint, coalition and allied forces. GCCS-M is implemented Afloat and at Ashore fixed command GCCS-Joint (GCCS-J) provides a fused picture of the battlespace within a modern command and control, communications and computer system that meets Joint warfighter and Distributed Command, Control & Communication (C3) needs. GCCS-J incorporates the core planning and assessment tools required by Combatant Commanders and their subordinate Joint Task Force Commanders to make accurate and timely decisions. GCCS-J is DoW's Joint Command and Control (C2) system of record and an essential component for successful implementation of the operational concepts of dominant maneuver, precision engagement, and full-dimension protection. GCCS-J provides situational awareness, imagery exploitation, indications and warning, collaborative planning, course-of-action development, intelligence mission support, and real-time combat execution capabilities needed to accelerate operational tempo and conduct successful military operations in the joint modern warfare environment in support of Pinnacle 27 and Fight from the Maritime Operations Center (FFTM) operations. FY27 funding also includes a one-time increase to support full hardware/software modernization of the current baseline capability at Joint Staff critical sites. This capability will provide real-time Common Operating Picture (COP) of the battlespace to support Joint and multi-national operations. [P5 / FA010 GCCS-M Afloat]: GCCS-M Afloat provides Command and Control capability to Force Level Ships (e.g. CVN Carriers, LCC Command Ships, LHA and LHD Amphibious Ships), Unit Level Ships (e.g. CG Cruisers, DDG Destroyers, MCM Mine Countermeasure Ships, LPD and LSD Amphibious Ships, FF/LCS Littoral Combat Ships, PC Coastal Patrol Ships), Submarines (e.g. SSN/SSBN/SSGN Submarines), the Software Support Activity (SSA), and the In-Service Engineering Activity (ISEA). [P5 / FA040 GCCS (Joint) Support Equipment]: Global Command and Control System- Joint (GCCS-J) is a Department of War (DoW) Program of Record managed by the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) GCCS-J Program Management Office (PMO). The GCCS-J system requirements, software release schedule, and system fielding plan are determined by the DISA GCCS-J PMO in coordination with the Joint Staff. GCCS-J supports the Joint Staff and Combatant Commanders by providing Command, Control, Communication, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) data processing capabilities, including status of forces and support requirements for use in national security decision making, force preparation and operational planning and execution. Global Command and Control System- Joint (GCCS-J) provides support for Fleet Communications Center interfacing with deployed units and other fixed Fleet and Joint Command Centers. There are currently 17 fielded and supported Navy GCCS-J Program of Record sites. [P5 / FA060 Joint Automated Deep Operations Coordination System (JADOCS)]: Provide funding for the Navy fielding of JADOCS software on new installation hardware. JADOCS is required to provide the capability to coordinate joint targeting and mission assignment for time sensitive targets and other rapid-response missions across Functional Component Commanders, Joint and Combined Force Commanders, Geographic Combatant Commanders, and Special Operations Commanders. Navigation Signal Timing and Ranging Global Positioning System (NAVSTAR GPS) provides assured and protected navigation solutions to Warfighters through supported, affordable, and integrated systems, and is the primary source of positioning, navigation and timing information for the Department of War (DoW). [P5 / (1R013) Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR)]: NAVWAR ensures that U.S. military forces maintain access to the GPS in an electronically challenging battlespace, delivers the capability to deny adversaries access to and use of GPS during military operations, and serves to preserve the peaceful use of GPS. Navy GPS Enhanced User Equipment (UE) Operational Requirements Document directs that future UE will incorporate an increased anti-jam capability. NAVWAR counters the threat by increasing resistance to intentional or unintentional interference. Sea NAVWAR Strategy is to install Increment 2 Advanced Digital Antenna Production (ADAP) antennas on surface platforms. The second increment also includes a smaller antenna variant for surface platforms with Size, Weight, Power and Cost (SWAP-C) restrictions. The ADAP antenna provides simultaneous dual frequency nulling and built in testability. Procurement and installation of anti-jam GPS antennas and modernized user equipment is required to ensure the continuation of GPS signals from space in a hostile jamming environment. The Sea NAVWAR program will equip ships with anti-jam GPS antennas to ensure the continued availability of GPS to support surface combat operations and provide reliable GPS and other positioning, navigation and timing data to ship-board Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C4ISR), [P3A / (1R019) Global Positioning System (GPS)-based Positioning, Navigation, & Timing Service (GPNTS)]: The GPS-based PNT Service (GPNTS) system is the primary PNT system for the Navy to ensure reliable PNT capability and interoperability insertion in GPS receivers and associated Command, Control, Computers, Communications and Intelligence (C4I) and Combat Systems in a denied environment. GPNTS provides more robust and secure GPS/PNT capabilities than is currently in the Fleet. GPNTS provides precise PNT data required for combat, weapons, command, control, communications, navigation, and other systems, as well as providing the time synchronization critical to the network environments. GPNTS backfits current PNT/GPS systems and forward fit new platforms. GPNTS is an Open Architecture (OA) development, enabling rapid software and hardware based capability improvements to be inserted without a requirement for single-source contracting. GPNTS will host the US Space Force developed Military GPS User Equipment (MGUE) card, allowing access to the new more accurate and secure GPS Military-Code (M-Code) signal. GPNTS also provides the capability to migrate non-real time GPS data toward a Common Computing Environment (CCE) and provide a path for the integration of advanced navigation systems and sensors. American Forces Radio and Television Service (AFRTS) shipboard systems provide command information to deployed Sailors and Marines and allow for the distribution of AFRTS programming in order to provide situational awareness for forward deployed commanders with real-time news and information. The systems also provide programming to Sailors and Marines at sea worldwide as a Navy Quality of Life (QOL) initiative, staying in compliance with the Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) Shipboard Habitability Program. These systems contribute significantly to the habitability of Navy ships by providing and distributing news, command information, training, and entertainment programming using the latest technology available. These systems improve morale, combat effectiveness and retention rates of deployed personnel. All AFRTS systems use Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) equipment. Fleet Support Detachments (FSDs) are the installing agents for these systems. Each component replacement is made based on ship availability, condition of system, and is coordinated through the Type Commanders (TYCOMs). [P5 / Site CCTV - Digital/300]: Shipboard Information, Training and Entertainment (SITE) Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Digital/300 is the next generation of the SITE 2000/300. This system is a digitally based replacement for the 2000/300 playback. Each system is comprised of Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) components that take three to twelve months to procure. Each component upgrade/replacement is made based on ship availability, by the Fleet Support Detachments (FSDs) as the installing/replacement agents and condition of the system. events.title: 1810N line 2820 Ashore ATC Equipment: FY2026 $97.262M, FY2027 $83.057M
events.text: 1810N line 2820 Ashore ATC Equipment: FY2026 $97.262M, FY2027 $83.057M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 6 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2820 / Ashore ATC Equipment (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) Marine Air Traffic Control and Landing Systems (MATCALS) provides for continuous, all-weather, radar/non-radar approach, departure, en-route, and tower air traffic control services to an aircraft. Marine Air Traffic Control (ATC) provides initial, transition and sustained air traffic support for the Joint and Marine Air Ground Task Force air operations in any environment. MATCALS satisfies the operational requirements set forth by Specific Operational Requirements 34-22 of 12 Jul 1973; and Air Traffic Navigation Integration and Coordination System ORD 05-002 of 03 Dec 1992. MATCALS, with other Marine Air Command and Control Systems (MACCS) and federal agencies, provides the ability to project air combat power without regard to weather. ATC automation reduces air traffic controllers' traffic handling and management time, allowing more time for mission response and task accomplishment. It supports a required increase in aircraft sortie rates and contributes to extended time on target. The system provides for integration of ATC into the total MACCS. To provide this capability, MATCALS consists of 4 primary subsystems: (1) Air Traffic Navigation integration and Coordination system (ATNAVICS) AN/TPN-31(V); (2) Expeditionary Control Tower AN/TSQ-120D; (3) the Man-Portable TACAN AN/TRN-47(V)1 & 3; (4) Transportable TACAN AN/TRN-47(V)2 & 4; and various ancillary equipment. This program works with the Marine ATC Working Group identifying the requirements to implement the Pre-Planned Product Improvement (P3I) and evolutionary product improvements as required for the Ground/Air Task-Oriented Radar (G/ATOR) system, Common Aviation Command and Control System (CAC2S), ATNAVICS, Expeditionary ATC Towers, and Navigational Aids that support Marine Air Traffic Control Companies. G/ATOR is a multi-role, ground-based, expeditionary radar that replaces five legacy radar systems for the Marine Air Ground Task Force. It satisfies the Marine Air Command and Control System (MACCS) and the Ground Counter Fire / Counter Battery capabilities. Integration of ATNAVICS with the CAC2S provides a coordinated and integrated set of equipment to provide enhanced Command and Control (AC2) capability for the Tactical Air Command Center, Tactical Air Operations Center, and Direct Air Support Center to support aviation employment in Joint, combined, and coalition operations. Increased MATCALS component obsolescence of aging systems is resulting in additional Maintainability, Reliability, Improvement (MRI) costs to support the changing operational environment of the MACCS as defined by USMC Force Design 2030 dated March 2020. Evolution of MATCALS to align with the overall USN/USMC North Star Precision Approach Landing Capability (PALC) to provide landing capability in both contested and non-contested environments via non-radar and radar based systems. The Joint DoW/Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) National Airspace System (NAS) Modernization (MOD) program upgrades the DoW ATC systems at approach control facilities in concert with the FAA's upgrade of the National ATC System. These funds will procure ATC systems for the Navy/Marine ATC facilities. The Air Force is the DoW lead activity for the Joint Acquisition Program. The Joint Program Office NAVAIR provides shore based ATC terminal facilities with equipment that is required in joint efforts to efficiently and safely monitor and direct military and commercial air traffic in national and international air space. Many of these systems are required to interface through automated means with the FAA. Additionally, NAVAIR has material support responsibility for Special Instrumentation Systems, and Ancillary Equipment used at Navy and Marine Corps Aviation Shore activities in the continental United States and overseas. Engineering Change Proposal (ECP)/Operational Capability Improvement Request (OCIR) modernization (MR069) - The ECP/OCIR program provides for the procurement and/or modification of critically needed communications, radar, displays, data processors, and other electronic systems/equipment at Navy/Marine Corps ATC facilities worldwide. ECP/OCIR procurements replace and modernize costly-to-maintain systems and equipment in order to increase ATC efficiency and safety, and reduce total ownership costs. UHF/VHF Antenna Upgrade (MR404) - This program procures and installs antenna, antenna towers, and antenna cables. Communications Systems Upgrade Program (MR408) - This program procures and installs advanced commercial state-of-the-art ATC voice switching equipment and was completed in FY 2019. Future upgrades and replacement systems will be performed under the NASMOD NAS Voice System budget line. UHF/VHF Transceiver Replacement Program (MR440) - This program modernizes aging Navy and Marine Corps UHF/VHF Transceivers that are the central core of all ATC emergency and Fleet Area Control & Surveillance Facility (FACSFAC) communications and was completed in FY 2019. Future upgrades and replacement systems will be performed under the NASMOD NAS Voice System budget line. Emergency Communication System (ECS) Upgrade Program (MR445) - This program modernizes obsolete and unsupportable ECS equipment. Voice Switches, Recorders, Reproducers, Uninterruptable Power Supplies, and Built-In Test Equipment will be replaced with modern, supportable components and procurements were completed in FY 2020 and installations completed in FY 2022. Future upgrades and replacement systems will be performed under the NASMOD NAS Voice System budget line. Air Field Lighting Control System (AFLCS) (MR510) - This program modernizes obsolete and unsupportable AFLCS equipment which will be replaced with modern, supportable components. events.text: 1810N line 2830 Afloat ATC Equipment: FY2026 $72.104M, FY2027 $62.581M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 4 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2830 / Afloat ATC Equipment (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) SATC systems are responsible for safe and expeditious control of air traffic within 50 Nautical Miles of a ship. SATC systems include the air traffic surveillance radar (ASR), AN/SPN43 and the air traffic control processing and display system, AN/TPX-42A(V), which has two major configurations: AN/TPX-42A(V)15/16. The (V)16 configurations comprise of Carrier Air Traffic Control Center - Direct Altitude and Identity Readout (CATCC-DAIR), Amphibious Air Traffic Control Center - Direct Altitude and Identity Readout (AATCC-DAIR); (V)16 DAIR system is used with the AN/SPN-43 and Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) inputs to track and control aircraft. The second configuration, AN/TPX-42A(V)15 interfaces with next generation multipurpose radars and IFF to perform the same mission. Obsolescence problems are being addressed through various upgrades in a phased approach. The major upgrades include a series of AN/TPX-42A(V) modification kits requiring various combinations of OL-541processor re-host, track processor upgrade, OD-220 console, audio/video recorder, flat panel display, embedded trainer, and other components to bring the AN/TPX-42A(V)16 through execution of the Air Traffic Control Multifunction Console Engineering Change Proposal (ECP), to the AN/SYY-1 configuration. The nomenclature AN/SYY-1 more accurately reflects the system attributes as a (S) water (Surface Ship), (Y) data processing, (Y) surveillance and control system. The ASR capability provided by the AN/SPN-43 radar system is required for NIMITZ Class CVNs and LHA/LHD class ships until the capability is replaced by the AN/SPN-50 Shipboard Air Traffic Radar. Obsolescence problems are being addressed through various upgrades in a phased approach until replaced. Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR) (AN/SPN-50(V)) The "National Defense Strategy of the United States of America" calls for military forces to assure allies and friends, dissuade potential adversaries, deter aggression and counter coercion, and defeat adversaries in order to accomplish our national objectives. The Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR) AN/SPN-50(V) supports these objectives and will be the primary Air Traffic Control (ATC) surveillance radar onboard Nimitz Class Aircraft Carrier (CVN) and Amphibious (LHA and LHD) type ships. The launch and recovery of aircraft, to include ATC, is a primary function of aircraft carriers and amphibious landing platforms. The surveillance function provides weather and radar data to air traffic controllers supporting aviation operations of all Navy, Marine Corps, joint and allied aviation assets within the assigned airspace. This data is utilized by air traffic controllers to provide a variety of ATC services such as ATC radar approach and departure services, which includes aircraft separation, airspace monitoring, navigational assistance, emergency vectoring, traffic calls, and vectoring and sequencing to the final approach point. Reliable and accurate ATC surveillance radar enhances overall mission and training effectiveness, and safety for aircrews and aircraft alike. The AN/SPN-50(V) CDD was signed March 2015 and Milestone B was achieved September 2015 where the Milestone Decision Authority (MDA) designated the AN/SPN-50(V) Program as an ACAT IV(T). The AN/SPN-50(V) CPD was signed November 2018. Milestone C was achieved September 2020, and IOC was achieved 3rd quarter FY 2024. The AN/SPN-50(V) inventory objective is 25 systems (20 LRIP and 5 FRP). ACLS Mod Kits comprises three legacy systems (AN/SPN-46, AN/SPN-41, and AN/SPN-35C) that provide the primary and secondary precision electronic guidance for landing suitably equipped aircraft under all weather conditions on CVNs, LHA/LHD class ships, and selected Naval Air Stations. Many of the components in the system have been in service for more than thirty years. This program funds maintainability, reliability, modernization and supportability improvements to existing equipment components that can no longer be maintained, procured or supported, as well as items providing upgraded capability and improved operational relevance in more environments. Life Cycle Extension (LCE) sustainment efforts for ACLS systems will be completed to address obsolescence and supportability issues, leverage Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) technology, address cyber-security updates and requirements, and support external system interface requirements. The LCE efforts by system are planned to be conducted in blocks, to address the most critical obsolescence, supportability, and emergent requirements first and to group remaining improvements into logical block upgrade packages that minimize multiple, duplicative repair efforts and reduce costs while delivering hardware in a time phased approach to meet ship maintenance availability schedules. This program includes a shore-based variant, installed at key airfields, that provides identical control signal indications (for pilot familiarization) as those provided by the afloat systems on board CVN vessels. In 2022, the Navy approved an updated Precision Approach and Landing Capability (PALC) Roadmap that planned to field system upgrades aimed at modernizing the AN/SPN-35 and AN/SPN-46 systems as well as inserting common sub-systems that minimize future sustainment costs. In 1QFY2025, the 2022 PALC Roadmap update was rescinded and the AN/SPN-51 development was halted. With no planned replacement system, it is essential to continue fielding Radar Landing System (RLS) mod kits that address subsystem obsolescence issues and extend the systems' life until a replacement system is identified. These mod kits support all three radar-based landing systems: AN/SPN-46 Automated Carrier Landing System (ACLS), AN/SPN-41 Instrument Carrier 2830 2027 Afloat ATC Equipment 1810N BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip

The Identification Systems program funds procurements and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) to address obsolescence and fact of life changes, installations, and certifications for the following Mark XII / Mark XIIA systems: AN/UPX-37, AN/UPX-41, AN/UPX-45 and AN/UPX-50 Digital Interrogators (DIs), AN/APX-118 and AN/APX-123 Common Digital Transponders (CXPs), AN/UPX-29 Interrogator System (comprised of Interrogator Set AN/UPX-24 or AN/UPX-49, OE-120/ UPX Antenna Group, and Mark XII or Mark XIIA equipment), AN/UPX-29 Modernization (UPneXt/Common Core), AN/UPX-46 Interrogator System (comprised of CP-2819/UPX Processor and Mark XIIA equipment), Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) support equipment, and AN/UPX-34A Radar Track Discriminator System (RTDS). The Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System, IFF, Mark XII/XIIA System (AIMS) is a Department of War directed tri-service program designed to provide a universal air traffic control radar beacon system compatible with the National Airspace System program. It provides a secure identification system for military use on all combatant ships, selected auxiliaries, patrol craft, and selected Coast Guard ships by allowing all friendly forces to identify each other and neutral forces. The Mark XII/XIIA system supports several missions such as anti-air warfare, aerial bombardment, and naval attack. The OE-120/UPX antenna radiates Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) encoded Radio Frequency (RF) challenge pulses into space and receives the resultant IFF encoded RF transponder replies from space. Current surface ship OE-120()/UPX antenna systems will receive upgrade kits to improve system R&M. The upgrade kits will use open architecture and current technology that allows for continued production and future growth. An Engineering Change Proposal was awarded using RDT&E (PU 0676) funds for the Original Equipment Manufacturer to deliver an Engineering Design Model for shipboard test and Modernization of the DDG 1000 Zumwalt Class IFF Sensor Suite includes procurement activities, product improvements, and engineering changes for three Electronically Scanned Array (ESA) antennas, one UPX-42(C) Interrogator, and three RT-1912(C)/APX Transponders. The hardware updates will reduce unique IFF configurations by installing common hardware with Mark XIIA capability. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) The Joint Precision Approach and Landing System (JPALS) is the primary precision approach and landing system for CVN and LHA/D ships to support aircraft without SPN-46 Automatic Carrier Landing Systems (ACLS) capability, which include F-35B, F-35C, MQ-25, CVM-22 and future platforms. The nomenclature for JPALS has been designated AN/USN-3(V)1, Satellite Signals Landing System (SSLS). JPALS ship systems are required to provide CVN and LHA/D ships a primary precision approach capability during night and instrument flight conditions, including coupled approach capability to a hover transition point for LHA/D ships, and coupled approach to the deck (auto-land) capability aboard CVN ships, and in contested environments. JPALS also provides over-the-air inertial alignment capability for CVN and LHA/D ships to support aircraft platforms without Link-4A capability, including F-35, MQ-25, CVM-22 and future platforms. JPALS MS B occurred June 2016 and MS C occurred April 2019. Production contract awarded May JPALS AN/USN-3 (V)2 upgrade is a GPS based precision approach landing capability in all weather and all operating environment for CVN and LHA/D ships. This supports contested environment operations for properly equipped manned and unmanned aircraft to include Air Wing of the Future (AWOTF). events.title: 1810N line 2876 Naval Mission Planning Systems: FY2026 $60.058M, FY2027 $54.487M
events.text: 1810N line 2876 Naval Mission Planning Systems: FY2026 $60.058M, FY2027 $54.487M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 5 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2876 / Naval Mission Planning Systems (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) This line item provides funding to procure Mission Planning workstations and associated Support Equipment, Software/Production Engineering Support, and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) for the Naval Mission Planning Systems (NavMPS) family of systems. The NavMPS family of systems includes the Joint Mission Planning System-Maritime (JMPS-M), Collaborative Mission Planning Continuum (CMPC) formerly called Next Generation Naval Mission Planning System (NGNMPS), JMPS-E (Expeditionary), Electronic Kneeboard (EKB), Common Munitions Built-in-Test (BIT)/Reprogramming Equipment (CMBRE), Standardized Tester of Reprogrammable Munitions (STORM, formerly called "Next Generation CMBRE"), and Common Munitions Built-in-Test (BIT)/Reprogramming Equipment Cyber Enhanced (CMBRE CE) JMPS-M (Maritime) is the legacy automated mission planning system for Naval Aviation, currently supporting over 40 Type/Model/Series (T/M/S) U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft and expeditionary forces. The JMPS-M program support includes platforms such as: F/A-18 A/B/C/D/E/F, EA-18G, CH-53K, Marine Helicopters, H-60 R/S, and P-8A. JMPS-M enables weapon system employment by providing the information and decision aids needed to rapidly plan aircraft, weapon or sensor missions, load mission data into aircraft and weapons, conduct mission rehearsal, and post mission analysis. The Naval Aviation's modern aircraft need data loaded from JMPS-M to fly their missions. The JMPS-M system procures hardware and software assets at all appropriate classification levels to support mission-planning requirements. The JMPS-M system is sun-setting in FY 2027 with a transition to CMPC. The Collaborative Mission Planning Continuum (CMPC) formerly called Next Generation Naval Mission Planning System (NGNMPS), will address critical capability gaps and deficiencies in the legacy JMPS that are required for modern 21st century integrated mission-centric and collaborative multi-domain mission planning, execution and analysis. The CMPC will begin replacing Naval Aviation's legacy JMPS no later than FY 2027 while also affordably leveraging prior investments across the systems of systems to deliver integrated and collaborative capability. The CMPC will address technological obsolescence while delivering enhanced capabilities to support the current Air Wing and the Air Wing of the future. The CMPC capability provides advanced multiple aircraft planning capabilities focused on emerging, high-threat mission areas. Current mission planning capabilities support individual aircraft and weapon initialization requirements. The emerging, near-peer threat environment demands a much more capable system that enables a team of aircraft to cooperate effectively across multiple mission areas, domains, and security levels. The CMPC will also leverage modernized architecture to provide revolutionary improvements in workflow, usability, cybersecurity. Additionally, CMPC will provide information and decision aids needed to rapidly plan/employ/maximize effectiveness of aircraft/weapon/sensor/payload mission plans. This functionality includes advanced pre-mission rehearsal/analysis, loading mission data into aircraft and weapons, dynamic replanning/retargeting against evolving threats in contested environments, and advanced post-mission debrief/ analysis. The CMPC will incorporate cross-domain solution capabilities. The CMPC system will also conduct work support advanced technology maturation, risk reduction activities, and system demonstrations supporting future mission planning needs for both USN and USMC users. These mission planning, mission execution, and mission analysis functions will be designed to meet the National Defense Strategy objectives. The CMPC will conduct preflight mission planning, data loading, rehearsals, mission execution and post mission analyses at all appropriate security classification levels. JMPS-E (Expeditionary) is a scalable, tailorable and collaborative web-based mission planning and execution monitoring tool for Marine Expeditionary Unit and Amphibious Squadron staffs embarked with each Amphibious Ready Group (ARG) and Expeditionary Strike Group (ESG). The EKB provides Naval Aviation with a scalable, rapidly deployable capability to support Department of War (DoW) digital transformation initiatives. The EKB is configured on a commercially available portable electronic device and contains digital flight information, aeronautical products, reference material, and flight planning tools to support aviation operations in land-based, littoral, and blue-water environments. The EKB also provides tactical mission planning and execution capabilities including tactical decision aids that support the range of Naval Aviation Enterprise (NAE) operations. The EKB has two baseline configurations - an unclassified Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) device and the Tactical Flight Bag (TFB) device, which is currently classified up to Secret after loading mission-specific software. The EFB's function is to support flight planning and execution while the TFB's function is to support tactical mission employment. The EKB effort addresses a high-priority fleet "paperless cockpit" initiative which reduces the number of printed paper-based products needed for in-flight use while also accommodating the need to store and display data to the operator necessary to execute training and tactical missions. EKB funding provides at least one operational EKB device per aircraft cockpit seat based on Primary Aircraft Authorization (PAA) requirements. The CMBRE system provides USN/USMC forces with the critical capability to perform built-in-test (BIT) and programming/reprogramming of various weapons both afloat and ashore. events.text: 1810N line 2900 Maritime Integrated Broadcast System: FY2026 $0.000M, FY2027 $0.000M BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip; 2 page(s); 1810N: Other Procurement, Navy / BA 02: Communications & Electronics Equip / 2900 / Maritime Integrated Broadcast System BSA 10: Other Shore Electronic Equipment (The following Resource Summary rows are for informational purposes only. The corresponding budget requests are documented elsewhere.) Funding for Maritime Integrated Broadcast System (MIBS) has been realigned out of line item 2900 into line item 2361 starting in FY 2026. This is to consolidate the number of program elements (PE) and budget line items (BLI) to group technology projects to allow flexibility fostering innovation and efficiency. PE/BLI consolidation meets the DoD Implementation Plan from the Commission on PPBE Final Report. The MIBS program delivers Integrated Broadcast Service (IBS) data to operational and tactical decision makers aboard United States Navy surface ships, shore headquarters, and other joint platforms. MIBS provides the Navy with the capability to receive and deliver near real time, Over the Air (OTA) IBS data, enhancing the Common Operation Picture (COP) supporting operations in all warfare areas. Including Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD), Anti-Air Warfare (AAW), Anti-Surface Warfare (ASUW), Undersea Warfare (UW), Electronic Warfare (EW) and track location of red and blue forces to warfighters at the tactical edge, regardless of Emission Control (EMCON) posture. MIBS provides essential support to the Over the Horizon-Targeting (OTH-T) mission and supports closure of the kill chain in a denied environment. This budget will provide a technical refresh of the Joint Tactical Terminal - Maritime (JTT-M) systems. The Joint Tactical Terminal - Maritime Evolved (JTT-ME) system replaces an End of Life (EoL) JTT- Senior terminals and infrastructure with a modern, secure, network enabled infrastructure that allows flexibility for future radios/waveforms. This system is formally specified by Fleet Commanders as a threshold capability for global Maritime Command, Control and Communications in a Distributed Maritime Environment to execute current Warfighting plans and is required for National Command and Control capability. The MIBS program will replace the End of Life (EoL) JTT-Senior radio (JTT-M) that has been in sustainment for 20+ years.
