events.text: SAM.gov sources sought 2026-08-25: Yard Diving Tender (YDT) Request for Information (RFI) request for information (sources sought); solicitation N0002426R2233; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/d35d8f171cf44fdaa6630288f3dd53ee?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 4ca8e73d3c88 PURPOSE: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime hereby issues a Request for Information (RFI) on behalf of the U.S. Navy and Foreign Military Sales, Boats, and Craft Program Office (PMS 300) to assess the availability of existing or in development craft designs applicable to the procurement of the attached requirements describing a Yard Diving Tender (YDT) craft. A prospective solicitation would seek to acquire two (2) YDTs to replace the YDTs currently in use with the Naval Diving and Salvage Training Center (NDSTC). This RFI will assist the Navy in finding qualified small business sources to build the required YDTs. Please note that only U.S.-built and U.S.-flagged vessels will be considered. The Navy intends to continue recapitalizing its aging fleet and procure YDTs beginning in Fiscal Year 2027. The overall objective of this Request for Information is to conduct and update market research to support preliminary planning for the acquisition of the YDT. The Navy plans to award a contract to one or more builders in FY27 for up to 2 crafts for delivery to the following: Panama City Beach, FL Description & MISSION PROFILE: The YDTs will be used by Naval Diving and Salvage Training Center (NDSTC), including Center for Explosive Ordnance Disposal & Diving (CENEODDIVE) to conduct training in underwater operations to locate, render safe and/or recover submerged objects and ordnance; harbor clearance/search; and expeditionary salvage operations. Through this RFI, the Navy aims to identify potential, commercial or developmental craft designs for the YDTs based on the following characteristics. Potential sources should have the personnel, facilities, technical capability and production capacity to produce up to two (2) YDTs. The Navy is particularly interested in existing, proven vessel designs that meet the following characteristics or that could be modified to meet the following characteristics while maintaining proven hull forms, propulsion systems and other major design features. Key YDT attributes and requirements: length: ≤52m (170ft) Beam: ≤10m (33ft) Draft: ≤3.6m Air Draft: ≤15m Cruise speed: ≥15 knots (at full load in Sea State 4) Range: ≥400 nautical miles at cruise speed Station Keeping: Dynamic Positioning class 2 (DP2) through Sea State 3, Beaufort Force 4 Sea State: Fully mission capable (including station keeping) up to Sea State 3, Beaufort Force 4 Fully mission capable (excluding station keeping) up to Sea State 4, Beaufort Force 5 Capable of restricted operations (transit at cruising speed) up to Sea State 5 Beaufort Force 6 Capable of surviving (maintaining course and heading) up to Sea State 6, Beaufort Force 7 Regulatory Bodies: American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) Marine Vessel Rules, U.S. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Title 33 and 46, U.S. Navy Diving Manual Deck Area: ≥180 square meters aft of deck house rated to carry payloads with concentrated local loads of up to 1500 kg/square meter Stability: ABS requirements for Intact and Damage Stability Personnel Capacity: ≥ 50 embarked persons Cranes: Aft deck crane ≥4,500 kg at 15 ft past deck edge Spaces (minimum requirement) Diving storage space: below the aft deck approximately 20 ft in length and the full width of the craft at a minimum Pilot House: full 360 degree field of view, command, control and navigation suite Crews Quarters: galley, messing and seating for 8, berthing for 4 Diving locker: ≥ 20 square meters located on main deck Passenger Space: Seating area with working surface for ≥42 persons for instruction and rest. Food storage and prep area and sufficient heads provided within or adjacent An additional 32 square meter enclosed compartment with access to the aft deck Responses & Submission of Information Interested parties are free to submit any information which may assist the Navy in its market research in response to this RFI. Responses to this RFI are limited to 10 pages and should include any relevant drawings, specifications, and/or sketches. The Government is not requesting a formal proposal at this time; however, please include as much of the technical data listed below as practical under the time constraints of this inquiry. As a reminder: please properly mark, clearly identify, and segregate any proprietary information included in your response. The following information is requested: Data and/or information on any vessel or vessel design in a similar size and capability range as that described in the draft specification. Data may be submitted on existing vessels, vessels that are conceptual or in design. If vessel is conceptual or in design, please provide level of maturity. A description of the company's relevant experience. Past experience performing construction of boats of similar dimensions and characteristics highlighting: construction techniques; portions of work which intended to be performed by the prime contractor and portions of work to be subcontracted, including identification of likely design agent; any intended teaming arrangements; and familiarity with Government contract requirements and drawing development. Examples of successful Government or commercial contracts of similar scope of work. A description of the boat design identified by the Contractor that meets or comes close to meeting the above listed design requirements. If applicable, identify the number of vessels and the years they were delivered. Provide approximate pricing for: Candidate vessel Delivery to stated location Engineering Cost Provide location of company production facilities. Describe facility production capacity ( e.g. , estimate on total construction time for one (1) YDT; how many YDTs can be built per year), based on current and projected yard-wide workload. The Navy recommends contractors to provide information demonstrating their capability/capacity for production throughput. events.title: SAM.gov sources sought 2026-08-26: Industry Day - Advanced Payload Integration Capabilities for Future Submarines
events.text: SAM.gov sources sought 2026-08-26: Industry Day - Advanced Payload Integration Capabilities for Future Submarines request for information (sources sought); solicitation N00024-26-R-6250; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/b2a6f595b1ba43d28c5acac1bd6dfb08?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 0ba889a48735 INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT Director, Submarine Programs (DSP) seeks industry input to advance payload integration capabilities for future submarines. The Director, Design & Construction (D,D&C) within Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager, Submarines (DRPM Subs) will host a classified, two-day Industry Day from Tuesday, September 29, 2026 (9:00 AM EST) to Wednesday, September 30, 2026 (12:00 PM EST) at Systems Planning and Analysis (SPA) 2001 N Beauregard St, Alexandria, VA 22311. This event will focus on existing, emerging, and feasible payload handling systems and payload/host-submarine integration challenges. Future submarines must support a wider variety of payloads than the current fleet. DSP is seeking specific technical solutions and concepts from industry to support the following areas: Logistics & operations : Onloading and offloading payloads above and below the waterline as well as logistics support of payloads underway. Launch and recovery systems for payloads during underway operations. Stowage & maintenance : Secured stowage, servicing, battery recharging, and maintenance of major payload components underway. Command, Control and Communications (C3) & ship control : Command and control of payloads and host ship during launch, recovery, and operations. Platform integration : Power, cooling, auxiliary system (e.g. hydraulics, fresh water) support, off-gassing considerations, and secure data exchange between payload and host ship systems. Safety & security : Onboard casualty response, anti-tamper, cybersecurity, and other security protocols. Lifecycle design : Launcher and payload system design for producibility and sustainment. Agenda Day 1: Briefings. The Government will brief attendees on future submarine requirements, capabilities, and mission profiles. The nuclear submarine shipbuilders (General Dynamics, Electric Boat and Huntington Ingalls Industries - Newport News Shipbuilding) will present concept designs focused on payload integration. Day 2: Breakout Sessions. Registered participants may request a 20-minute, one-on-one session with Government, shipbuilder, warfare center, and UARC personnel to discuss technical concepts, industry capabilities, and receive feedback on design feasibility. Note: Do not submit generic capability statements. DSP is only seeking specific technical solutions and ideas for future submarine payload integration. To view additional items and information for this opportunity, please navigate to: https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil/ and request access to the 'E-TIC - Industry Engagement' folder. Please note the following mandatory access requirements: A verified AIMTC account is required. AIMTC account registration is available for personnel without an active account. An active DISS (Defense Information System for Security) clearance is required to gain access to the ETIC platform. Please ensure you meet these security and credential requirements prior to attempting to view the documents. E-TIC folder will be free to access from 08/26/2026 to 09/30/2026. This notice is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP) and the Government is not requesting or accepting proposals currently. There is no obligation for potential offerors to respond to this notice. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS & ACCESS CONTROL Classification Level: All briefings, discussions, and breakout sessions will be conducted at the SECRET//NOFORN level Clearance Verification: All attendees must be U.S. citizens and possess a final, active U.S. SECRET (or higher) security clearance. Interim clearances will not be accepted for facility access. Visit Authorization Request (VAR) Submission: In addition to registering via email, a formal VAR must be submitted via the Defense Information System for Security (DISS). Host Facility: SPA SPA SMO Code: 7L563 Purpose of Visit: DRPM Subs / DSP Future Submarine Payload Integration Industry Day Point of Contact: Mr. Joshua Engle (joshua.engle@spa.com or 571-771-0859) Date of Visit: September 29, 2026, to September 30, 2026 Note: VARs must be received and verified in DISS no later than August 28, 2026. Attendees without an approved VAR in DISS will be denied entry to the SPA facility. REGISTRATION PROCESS (TWO-STEP VERIFICATION) To participate in this event, companies must complete both of the following steps by 28 August 2026: Step 1: Email Registration. Email Mr. Matt Hedrick at matthew.c.hedrick.civ@us.navy.mil with the subject line: "DSP Payload Integration Industry Day Registration - [Company Name]". In this email, please provide: Primary Point of Contact (Name, Email, Phone Number). Company/Organization Name and Address. Names of the participating individuals (maximum of 3 per company). An explicit request for a Day 2 One-on-One Breakout Session (if desired). Note: Attendance is limited to three (3) representatives per organization, with exceptions granted for designated Industry Day presenters as approved by the PMS 351 Program Office. Step 2: DISS VAR Submission. Submit a formal Visit Authorization Request via DISS utilizing the SMO code and details listed in the Security Requirements section above. FACILITY RULES & SECURITY PROTOCOLS Identification: Each attendee must present a valid, unexpired U.S. government-issued photo ID (e.g., CAC, Military ID, or U.S. Passport) at the check-in desk. Prohibited Devices: SPA is a classified facility. Absolutely no electronic devices, wearable technology, or recording-capable hardware will be permitted inside the briefing or breakout rooms. This includes, but is not limited to: Mobile phones and tablets Smartwatches and fitness trackers (e.g., Apple Watch, Fitbit) Laptops and electronic storage media (USBs, external hard drives) Cameras, voice recorders, and Bluetooth-enabled devices Smart Glasses Storage: Limited secure storage lockboxes may be available at the facility entrance, but attendees are highly encouraged to leave prohibited electronic devices in their vehicles. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections & assessments, engineering & design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government's facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections & assessments, engineering & design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Government's facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. The solicitation will be issued electronically via System for Award Management (SAM) at http://sam.gov and interested parties must comply with that announcement. Interest offerors should monitor the SAM.gov page for any applicable amendments to this solicitation. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management in order to participate in this procurement at https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM/. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which shall be considered by the agency. SAM.gov is the single point of entry for posting of the synopsis and solicitations to the internet. This pre-solicitation notice is for information purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to solicit contractual offers or award of contracts. The Government is not soliciting, nor will it accept, proposals as a result of this synopsis. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided as a result of this notice. The solicitation is forthcoming.

events.text: SAM.gov combined synopsis/solicitation 2026-09-01: Apple MacBook Pro laptops solicitation (combined synopsis); solicitation N0017326Q5624-1; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/be2e35a56f29401bbf93b6794322ede6?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 c171879d9d8a This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.6, "Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items," as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is a Request for Quotations (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 Effective: 13MARCH2026 This is a Total Small Business Set-Aside in accordance with FAR 13.003 (b)(1) on a Firm-Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) basis. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334111 , with a small business size standard of # 1250 . The associated Federal Supply Code (FSC) / Product Service Code (PSC) procurement is 7A21 . The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL), located in Washington, DC, is seeking to purchase Apple Macbook Pro . All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: __x____ See specification attachment RFQ N0017326Q5624-2 is hereby issued as the updated and controlling solicitation and supersedes the previous RFQ N0017326Q5624. Offerors shall rely solely on the terms, conditions, clauses, attachments, and submission instructions contained in RFQ N0017326Q5624-2. This updated RFQ adds the following FAR clauses/provisions: FAR 52.225-1, Buy American—Supplies FAR 52.225-2, Buy American Certificate FAR 52.219-6, Notice of Total Small Business Set-Aside Offerors are responsible for reviewing the updated RFQ and submitting quotations in accordance with RFQ N0017326Q5624-2. Supplies: BRAND NAME ONLY Items must be brand name only in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(3) The Government has determined that only the specified brand-name item will satisfy the agency's minimum requirements. Software/Hardware/Services : This procurement is for new equipment ONLY, unless otherwise specifically stated. No remanufactured or "gray market" items are acceptable. All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer's warranty. • Vendor shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), an OEM authorized dealer, an authorized distributor, or an authorized reseller for the proposed equipment/system such that OEM warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty, and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions • Offerors are required to submit documentation from the manufacturer stating that they are an authorized distributor for the specific items being procured. Note: Maintenance Renewals - The performance period for maintenance renewals, (software licenses, services, etc.), must begin on or after the date of contract award. The performance period cannot be back dated. If reinstatement fees are required, they must be listed on separate line items. This requirement for submission must comply with applicable FAR clauses. FAR 52.225-1 Buy American-Supplies FAR 52.225-2 Buy American Certificate FAR 52.219-6 Notice of Total Small Business Set-Aside Delivery Address: ____X____ U.S. Naval Research Laboratory 4555 Overlook Avenue, S.W. Bldg. 49 - Shipping/Receiving Code 3400 Washington, DC 20375 **FOB DESTINATION IS THE PREFERRED METHOD** Estimated Delivery Time: __________________ For FOB ORGIN, please provide the following information: FOB Shipping Point: _______________________ Estimated Shipping Charge: _________________ Dimensions of Package(s): ____________________ Shipping Weight: __________________________ SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: All Quoters shall submit 1 (one) copy of their technical and price quote. Include your company DUNS Number and Cage Code on your quote. All quotations shall be sent via e-mail. GOVERNMENT POINT OF CONTACT Purchasing Agent Name: Andrea Graves Tel: 202-875-9251 Email: andrea.l.graves6.civ@us.navy.mil Please reference this combined synopsis/solicitation number on your correspondence and in the "Subject" line of your email. ALL QUESTIONS REGARDING THE SOLICITATION SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. The government intends to award a purchase order as a result of this combined synopsis/solicitation that will include the terms and conditions set forth herein. Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors should have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. events.title: SAM.gov sources sought 2026-09-02: PMS 300 Naval Surface Warfare Center - Carderock (NSWCCD) Acoustic Research Deta
events.text: SAM.gov sources sought 2026-09-02: PMS 300 Naval Surface Warfare Center - Carderock (NSWCCD) Acoustic Research Deta request for information (sources sought); solicitation N00024-26-R-2234; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/110d2c4495fc45dda8ee255f74a11360?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 0c17f2fa780f PURPOSE: This combined Request for Information (RFI)/ Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is being issued by the U.S. Navy, Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime code PMS 300, as market research to assess industry interest and identify capable sources through collecting capability statements for the acquisition of one (1) Research Vessel (R/V) for NSWC Carderock Acoustic Research Detachment (NSWCCD ARD). The Navy is providing notional planning schedules and technical requirements to assist industry in developing responses and to solicit feedback of the requirement. Submission of any information in response to this announcement is purely voluntary. This RFI/SSN does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future SCOPE: Research Vessel (R/V): The anticipated plan for future procurement against this requirement is the PAE Maritime, Deputy PAE Expeditionary & Mine Warfare, PMS 300 Service Craft & Boats Multi-Award Contract (SCB MAC). Interested parties may respond following the guidance below in "RESPONSES & SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION" section. The notional schedule listed below is provided for planning purposes only. The descriptions and key characteristics of the potential service craft and boats are provided herein. The Government is not obligated to pursue this schedule or a future solicitation because of this RFI/SSN. Issue Industry RFI 4rd QTR FY26 Conduct Industry Day 1st QTR FY27 Issue Draft RFP 2nd QTR FY27 Release Final RFP 2nd QTR FY27 Anticipated Award 3rd QTR FY27 DESCRIPTIONS Acoustic self-noise data collection for the U.S. Navy is performed at the Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division's (NSWCCD) Acoustic Research Detachment (ARD) in Bayview, ID on Lake Pend Oreille (LPO). Such testing requires a vessel with a combination of size, speed, acoustic signature, and towing capability to accurately assess the performance of the towed arrays without interference from the host vessel. Primary mission of this R/V is to support testing on towed Sonar arrays and replace the aging R/V Chinook . Workboat Key Characteristics: Boat Type - Research /Vessel (R/V) Notional Dimensions - 80 ft maximum length 22' beam maximum ~ 8' molded depth; 6' side height (actual) ~16'-5" bottom width Propulsion - Marine Diesel propulsion plant (must meet requirements as specified in "Notional Speed"). Bow Thrusters for maneuverability on Lake Pend Oreille. Notional Speed - Minimum speed: 2 kts Cruising Speed: 12-15 kts Max tow speed: 30 kts Max transit speed: 35 kts Crew - Crew Size: Four (4) personnel; 200ft allotment/room for staffed computer lab (12 personnel) vice passenger compartment. Galley and heat required, including hands-free Collection, Holding and Transfer ( CHT) system for offboarding waste if possible. Other Notional Characteristics - Required vertical deck payload 30,000 lbs. and 20,000 lbs. tow load for various towed arrays and on-deck cable reels of varying sizes and weights. Requires specialized acoustic treatments including items specified immediately below this table for NSWCCD ARD to complete test events and analysis. General Must be delivered direct to ARD's facility in Bayview, ID. Vessel must have a four-point mooring system for movement/transportation via overhead crane. Computer Lab must have crane port via deckhead to enable placement and removal of systems within the Lab space. Acoustic Treatments: Single isolation mounts for all normally operating rotating or reciprocating machinery in the engine room, propulsion motor room, and auxiliary machinery spaces. Local damping on foundations of the propulsion motors and several other key auxiliaries in the engine room and propulsion motor room. Acoustic damping for power generators. Masker (new or retrofit). Electronics LiDAR, RADAR, ADCP, USCG-compliant Marine Radio, Intercom and Depth Sounder. Weather Station. Generator One (1) 40 KW, 120/208 volt 3-phase 60 hertz generator One (1) 60 KW, 120/208 volt 3-phase 60 hertz generator Backup redundancy in case of generator casualties Electrical power filtering for Computer Lab electronics RESPONSES & SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: Interested parties are invited to submit any information that may support the Navy's market research efforts. If interested and capable to perform the above described efforts, please provide the following information on company letterhead: 1) Organization name, address, e-mail address, web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming (>20%) is anticipated to deliver technical and industrial capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. Respondents are responsible for properly marking and clearly identifying proprietary information or trade secrets contained within their response. The Government will not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for any proprietary information not properly marked and clearly identified. Information provided shall be treated as Business Sensitive and will not be shared outside of Government activities and agencies without the permission of the provider. Do NOT provide classified information or use the marking "CONFIDENTIAL". BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS RFI/SSN THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. In accordance with FAR 52.219-14, should the prospective contract be competed as a small business set aside, the prospective offeror would be required to perform 50% of the cost of manufacturing, to include industrial work, planning, engineering, and program management. If you are a small business, include a description of your plan to meet the requirements within the capability statement portion of your submission.

events.text: SAM.gov presolicitation 2026-09-02: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Antenna Control System presolicitation (intent to solicit); solicitation N00173-26-RFI-GD01; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/68f739dd386c45b681bb3eae0161eeeb?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 3ac5c09f882e Performance Location: Contractors Facility The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) intends to award a firm-fixed-price purchase order in accordance with FAR 12.102 to CPI Satcom & Antenna Technologies Inc. located in Plano, Texas. The Government intends to procure one (1) Model 990 Antenna Control System (ACS) with associated equipment and installation, in accordance with the attached salient characteristics. This sole source requirement meets the conditions of 41 U.S.C. 1901(e)(2) as implemented by FAR 12.102. The required ACS is required to be compatible with the mechanical, electrical, and network architecture of a twin AN/FSC-78 Antenna System ACS already in use at the same Facility. Specifically, the ACS to be acquired must be compatible with the Facility's existing AN/FSC-78 ACS hardware and software network architecture. Interested companies may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals and does not constitute a solicitation. However, all capability statements received prior to the closing date shall be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. If your organization has the capability of performing these services NRL asks that interested parties, at a minimum, supply the below information. Submissions not containing all of the below information will not be considered. Business name and address; Name of company representative, business title and email; Telephone number, address, and e-mail address of POC; Large or Small Business Size and Type of Small Business (if applicable); Cage Code; UEID Number; A brief capabilities statement package (no more than five pages) demonstrating their ability to perform the services required under this posting. Demonstrated past performance providing similar services should be detailed, if applicable. A detailed analysis of how your firm will successfully remove the sole source barriers listed above. events.title: DON26BZ06-DV088 DIRECT TO PHASE II: Minimally Invasive Remote Blood Collection Device for Free-Ranging Cetaceans
events.text: DON26BZ06-DV088 DIRECT TO PHASE II: Minimally Invasive Remote Blood Collection Device for Free-Ranging Cetaceans SBIR topic DON26BZ06-DV088, DoW SBIR 2026 BAA, Pre-Release; opens 2026-09-23, closes 2026-10-21; Adapt an existing capillary blood collection device initially designed for humans and develop prototype hardware for use on Fleet dolphins and free-ranging cetaceans of varying epidermal thickness to improve proactive marine mammal monitoring, health measurements, and insight into behavioral responses to ensure ongoing mission reliability of Navy operations. Navy bottlenose dolphins are valuable Fleet assets whose health and well-being are essential to sustaining mine countermeasures, port security, and object recovery missions. Medical issues compromise performance and have direct implications for Navy mission readiness, longevity, and reliability. Additionally, for the U.S. Navy to meet environmental compliance requirements under the Marine Mammal Protection Act and Endangered Species Act, it is essential to understand the effects of sound and military activity on marine mammals, including physiological, behavioral, ecological, and population-level effects. While technologies and techniques for assessing marine mammal health are growing rapidly, many barriers remain for these Fleet assets as well as other free-swimming large cetacean species that can be used as biological sensors of the undersea environment. A transformative diagnostic tool will provide unparalleled access to physiological data and biomarkers of health, stress, and disease from free-swimming cetaceans with applications in clinical care, operational biosurveillance, and conservation. Blood sampling of captive trained dolphins and/or stranded marine mammals enables researchers to evaluate individual and population health, age, genetics, exposure to pathogens and toxicants, and physiological responses to anthropogenic and natural stressors. By enabling minimally invasive blood sampling in free-ranging cetaceans, these animals can be used as biological sensors for persistent surveillance of the undersea environment, providing early warning of pathogens and other ecosystem stressors in operational waters. However, current blood collection methods in marine mammals are designed for use on stranded or captured individuals and are therefore limited in their capability of rapidly assessing health for larger free-swimming species. The lack of such a tool for health assessments is particularly urgent for Fleet animals and free-ranging animals in the region of deployment, where timely and accurate health assessments are essential for informing recovery efforts and mitigating population decline. As such, there is a critical need for a minimally invasive blood collection tool for remote application to the skin of free-ranging cetaceans to address significant gaps and improve our understanding of marine mammal health across spatiotemporal scales, providing unprecedented data on physiological responses, health metrics, and population dynamics. This SBIR Direct to Phase II topic seeks to develop a prototype minimally invasive blood collection device for remote application on free-ranging cetaceans by further developing an existing capillary blood collection device initially designed for humans. This prototype device should be able to be remotely deployed using current techniques used for the deployment of suction-cup electronic tags on free-ranging marine mammals (i.e., pole-based or drone dropped) under diverse environmental conditions. This prototype will include a blood collection device, waterproof housing, delivery device using suction cup tag carrier, and suction cup-based tag attachment. This prototype waterproof device should be capable of remotely deployable blood collection across cetacean species of varying epidermal thickness. The target size and weight of the blood collection device (not including the suction cup housing) should be approximately 3.40x2.25x1.30 in in size and weigh between 0.85 and 0.95 oz. This prototype device should sit flush and seal against the skin and use suction to draw 200-800 uL of capillary blood with minimal clotting into an internal reservoir (independent of orientation) and mix the sample with anticoagulants or other stabilization chemicals. At minimum the Phase II prototype should be able to collect blood samples from species with epidermis of < 2.5 mm thickness with a plan to successfully collect blood samples from species with epidermal thickness of > 10 mm. During this collection period, the device needs to make a narrow incision (< / = 0.15 mm in width, < 5 mm in length) such that rapid wound healing is possible. Further, the device needs to account for pressure variations underwater such that it detaches from the animal after a set time (< 3 minute duration) or when it reaches a critical depth or, at a minimum, be able to identify samples that may have ex vivo red cell hemolysis. In addition, the device will need to protect the blood sample from seawater intrusion. Blood samples collected via this prototype device need to have comparable blood test values to those collected via standard venipuncture methods through the Peri-Arterial Venous Rete (PAVR). As such, to optimize reliable blood collection from the prototype device, development must address challenges including clotting, lancing depth, and anticoagulant use. This minimally invasive blood collection prototype device will result in reliable remote deployment on free swimming cetaceans and significantly improve the capability to assess physiological responses and health measures in cetacean populations across spatial and temporal ranges. For the Navy Fleet bottlenose dolphins in particular, this prototype device will enhance the ability to detect health changes, reduce unplanned medical stand-downs, and provide more continuous health oversight by providing a minimally invasive diagnostic tool to detect infection and inflammatory markers, as well as subclinical infections. It will offer a novel tool to enhance systemic and organ-specific health monitoring, providing individualized biomarker data that can be applied to preventive med 2026-09-23 2026-10-21 DOD_SBIR_2026_P1_CBZ ONR SBIR blood sampling; blood collection; minimally invasive; health assessments; marine species health; rapid health assessment DON26BZ06-DV088

events.title: SAM.gov presolicitation 2026-09-08: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing
events.text: SAM.gov presolicitation 2026-09-08: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing presolicitation (intent to solicit); solicitation N0003926RR002; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/8fc4045217f64e1c80bb9160b12a3716?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-21 sha256 2bd5bb631380 The Department of the Navy Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) / Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) hereby issues this announcement regarding a forthcoming Area of Interest (AOI) for Medium Unmanned Surface Vehicles (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing. MUSV uses modular design principles to create adaptable and resilient solutions that can effectively counter evolving threats. We invite interested parties with expertise in innovative solutions to complex problems, vessel construction, autonomy, perception systems, and general maritime experience to participate in this opportunity. Vendors will be evaluated on platform maturity, open-architecture autonomy compatibility, endurance, payload integration capacity, and rapid-production scalability. To meet the critical operational demand signal for high-volume autonomous vessel procurement over the next decade, DRPM RAS will employ innovative and streamlined acquisition pathways. The government will leverage the authorities of 10 U.S.C. 3458 (Commercial Solutions) and 10 U.S.C. 4022 (Other Transactions) and intends to award Basic Ordering Agreements and prototype other transaction agreements, and potentially production contracts or transactions to successful vendors. To maintain technical superiority and capture rapid commercial innovations, DRPM RAS intends to issue the AOI with a rolling open window. This open call will allow new entrants to compete and existing vendors to submit updated product blocks and modular payload configurations. Approved platforms will be accepted into the maritime marketplace hosted on drones.mil. This digital clearinghouse will empower authorized acquisition authorities and operational stakeholders across the Department of War enterprise to rapidly configure and issue funded delivery orders for vetted maritime autonomous systems without redundant procurement cycles. Formal AOI release is planned on or before September 30, 2026. Detailed AOI instructions will be released via SAM.gov and syndicated at https://drones.mil. Interested industry vendors capable of delivering commercial or dual-use maritime unmanned surface systems are encouraged to ensure active SAM.gov registrations and monitor this notice for amendments, industry day announcements, and formal AOI documentation. All inquiries concerning this notice must be submitted in writing to the Agreements Officer at Christopher.j.murr.civ@us.navy.mil (note this email is distinct/different than the auto generated SAM.gov).

This Signature Availability includes a combination of maintenance, modernization, and repair, and will require highly capable contractors with substantial facilities, to include capable pier (for the applicable ship class) as well as human resources capable of completing, coordinating, and integrating multiple areas of ship maintenance, repair and modernization. This Signature Availability is solicited on a coast-wide basis on the West Coast under a single solicitation, and one (1) contract to complete the availability is expected to be awarded to one (1) contractor. Based on the complexity, magnitude and duration of the requirement, the Governments market research indicates there are not two or more small business concerns capable of competing for these requirements and therefore this procurement will not be set aside for small business (FAR 19.502-2(b)). This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested parties must comply with this announcement. Interested offerors should monitor the PlEE.gov and SAM.gov pages for the release of the solicitation and any applicable amendments, thereafter. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to participate in this procurement at https://www.sam.gov. All responsible sources may submit a proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to all applicable CDRLs, J- and S- attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Jacob Juros at jacob.a.juros.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Brian Romano, at brian.c.romano.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your companys SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. ***NOTICE*** In addition, there are references that contain limiting distribution statements and will not be disseminated from the Contract Specialist. In these instances, Offerors shall contact the Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) Technical Librarian at swrmc.techdocs@us.navy.mil to arrange access per RFP Section L instruction. Offerors shall review Section L, General Information for further details. ***END NOTICE***The Government anticipates making a single award in or before March 2027. USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 DSRA will begin in November 2027 with an expected completion in October 2029.

This process is repeated in order of price until an offer or combination of offers is deemed technically acceptable and price is determined fair and reasonable. Options. events.text: SAM.gov sources sought 2026-09-16: Advanced GNSS Simulator request for information (sources sought); solicitation N0017326RFIMA01; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/b85a3523e117427facad43affeddf165?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 4264c42c5253 *****This announcement is not a formal Request for Quotes (RFQ). This SSN/RFI is for informational and planning purposes only and does not guarantee that an award will be made. Any quotes submitted in response to this SSN/RFI are not quotes on which an order will be issued. The Government assumes NO financial responsibility for any costs incurred. A solicitation package is not available at this time. However, should such a requirement materialize, no basis for claims against NRL shall arise as a result of a response to this SSN/RFI or NRL's use of such information either as part of our evaluation process or in developing specifications or work statements for any subsequent requirement. PURPOSE AND ACQUISITION BACKGROUND The purpose of this notice is to identify potential industry sources capable of delivering a high-precision, multi-channel Advanced Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Simulator suite. This requirement will support critical Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) research, development, and testing spanning dual-frequency GPS baselines, encrypted military signals (SAASM and AES M-Code), full-spectrum multi-constellations, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Alternative Navigation (ALTNAV), lunar S-band PNT, contested/threat environments, and multi-element Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) wavefront testing. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS & TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS The required capability consists of a minimum of two (2) discrete simulation units meeting the essential physical, electrical, and functional characteristics detailed below. Essential Physical and Electrical Characteristics (Applicable to Both Units) Essential Physical Characteristics Mounts in standard width 19-inch rack mount and includes mounting brackets. Mountable rack units less than or equal to 27 inches of depth. Stable operation over temperature range of 10degC to 40degC and 40% to 90% relative humidity, non-condensing. RF output ports are located on front and rear of chassis and are Type N female connector. RF connector ports are all 50-ohm impedance. Minimum of one combined RF output Type N female connector for high-power generation (+50dB above nominal). BNC female connector for 1 Pulse Per Second (PPS) input for syncing to external pulse. BNC female connector for 1 Pulse Per Second (PPS) output from simulator to provides a precise hardware timing reference signal of the simulated UTC second. BNC female connector for trigger input port to start or synchronize a scenario run. BNC female connector for an external 10 MHz reference input. BNC female connector for 10Mhz internal reference output. At least four (4) Universal Serial Bus (USB Type-A, 3.0 or higher) ports on rear panel and 2 USB (Type-A, 3.0 or higher) ports on front panel for I/O connections. At least one video interface option must be DisplayPort (DP 1.4a or higher) or High-Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI 2.1 or higher). Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0 or higher included on computer to address Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) requirements. Essential Functional Characteristics (Operational, Behavioral, Software Capabilities) At a minimum, two separate units are needed. The first unit must simulate the constellations listed below and simulate a receiver in a stationary (static) position or in a moving (dynamic) position either on the earth or in a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) around the earth. Global Positioning System (GPS) - including the Selective Availability Anti-spoofing Module (SAASM) classified package and M-code L1 - 1575.42MHz L2 - 1227.6MHz L5 - 1176.45MHz Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS) L1 - 1598.06MHz to 1609.31MHz L2 - 1242.9375MHz to 1251.6875 MHz BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) B1I - 1561.098MHz B2I - 1207.14MHz Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System E1 - 1575.42MHz E5a - 1176.45MHz E5b - 1207.14MHz E6 - 1278.52MHz Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) L5 - 1176.45MHz S-band - 2492.028MHz QZSS L1 - 1575.42MHz L2 - 1227.6MHz L5 - 1176.45MHz Alternative Navigation (ALTNAV) Simulate Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite signals used for commercial and military alternative navigation. Emulates non-GNSS radio frequency sources, including ground-based transmitters. Lunar PNT 2483.5 - 2500 MHz S-band range, XONA Space system emulation X1 - 1591.2MHz - 1595MHz X5 - 1180.4MHz - 1200.6MHz • Integrated commercial low Earth orbit (LEO) production signals bundle software (designed specifically to generate and test next-generation LEO-based PNT waveforms such as Xona). System 2 (Multi-Output & Secure PNT for CRPA Testing) The second unit must simulate only the GPS constellation below and still simulate a receiver in a stationary position(static) or in a moving(dynamic) position either on the earth or in a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) around the earth. Global Positioning System (GPS) - including the Selective Availability Anti-spoofing Module (SAASM) classified package and M-code L1 - 1575.42MHz L2 - 1227.6MHz L5 - 1176.45MHz • Minimum of 4 element Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) testing capability. The platform is required to emulate the synchronous, phase coherent and spatially correct RF wavefront as received at each element of a CRPA. REQUIRED CONTRACTOR RESPONSE FORMAT: Interested parties, at a minimum, shall supply all of the below required information in a Capability Statement. 1. CONTACT INFORMATION: a) Company Name and Address b) Point of Contact for questions/clarification c) Telephone Number and e-mail address d) CAGE Code, and business size e) NAICS and PSC Code of the proposed solution (SEE https://psctool.us) f) Business Size Standard /Socioeconomic Categories 2. TECHNICAL INFORMATION: a) List of capabilities/resources relevant to the above specifications. b) Questions for the Technical team regarding changes/suggestions to the specification list to add clarity. events.text: SAM.gov solicitation 2026-09-22: Low Profile Mast and Rotational Module Component Prototype Other Transaction Are area of interest under a commercial solutions opening (solicitation); solicitation N00024-26-R-6215; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/47e1c5d28e634633bcdf0820327d6a3c?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 23125fbac152 Team Submarines, Australia, United Kingdom, and United States (AUKUS), International & Systems (AI&S), Submarine Electromagnetic Systems Program Office (PMS 435) is pleased to release a competitive Area of Interest (AOI) announcement for the Low Profile Mast (LPM) and Rotational Module (RM) component to address several key operational needs. The LPM/RM programs seek innovative technologies that accelerate the prototyping of capabilities that address these key operational needs. To accelerate the design, development and demonstration of LPM/RM capabilities, the Navy will be utilizing the Other Transaction Authority pathway outlined in Title 10 U.S.C. § 4022. It is intended that this solicitation may result in the award of one or more prototype projects. There are nine (9) attachments to this AOI, some of which contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): LPM/RM Terms of Use Agreement AOI AOI Guidance CUI LPM Type 24 Mod 1Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI LPM Verification Guide (VG) [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Verification Guide [RESTRICTED] LPM/RM AOI Questions Form CUI LPM/RM Placemat Template [RESTRICTED] Companies are advised to proceed with the following steps to respond to this notice: STEP 1 - Terms of Use Agreement (TOU) Several key documents related to the LPM Type 24 Mod 1 and RM are only releasable to eligible businesses with ownership in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Non-Australia, United Kingdom, or United States foreign-owned businesses may submit a technical solution as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more Australia, United Kingdom, or United States-owned businesses. The ability to be awarded an Agreement may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain access to restricted information. Companies interested in submitting a technical solution in response to the AOI shall complete Attachment 1: TOU Agreement and return it via e-mail to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialists listed in this notice. The Company point of contact that will request access to the restricted documents in this notice shall be the Company point of contact listed in the TOU. Companies should also request access to the restricted CUI documents in SAM at the time of TOU submittal to the Government. Once the signed TOU is received and verified, Team Submarines will grant access to the restricted CUI documents and transmit relevant UNCLASSIFIED Government-Furnished Information (GFI) relevant to the AOI to the Company point of contact listed in the TOU. NOTE: The TOU provided as Attachment 1 is specific to this AOI release; if a Company previously submitted a TOU under prior LPM/RM Industry Day notice, that Company must submit a separate TOU for this AOI opportunity. STEP 2 - QUESTIONS & ANSWERS OPPORTUNITY Companies may submit questions using Attachment 8: LPM/RM AOI Questions Form. Team Submarine will only accept Q&A submissions up to the CUI level. Q&A submissions shall be submitted electronically via e-mail to the Government points of contact listed in this notice no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 2, 2026 . -SUBJECT: N00024-26-R-6215 Q&A This opportunity is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or for the information provided in response to this notice. The Government may or may not respond to Q&A submissions and reserves the right to redact the content of submissions prior to any release back to industry. The Government may use the information and feedback provided in Q&A submissions to inform future solicitations as necessary. Respondents are solely responsible for properly marking and clearly identifying any proprietary information or trade secrets contained in any submission in response to this notice. Opting not to submit any Q&A does not preclude participation in this AOI or any future engagements. It is the responsibility of industry to monitor the Government Point of Entry (GPE) for official AOI communications. STEP 4 - Companies shall submit Phase I White Papers and Placemats electronically via encrypted DoD SAFE transmission. Companies must request a DoD SAFE link by e-mailing ALL Government points contract listed in this notice no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 13, 2026. -SUBJECT: [insert LPM or RM] N00024-26-R-6215 DoD SAFE Link [insert COMPANY NAME] If a Company intends to send a Phase I submission for both LPM and RM, that Company must request two separate DoD SAFE links. Companies are encouraged to submit White Papers prior to the latest closing date. Inclusion of a delivery receipt with an email submission will be the only indication of the Government's successful receipt of a White Paper. Each Company must comply with DoD SAFE file size limitations and other guidance as provided at https://safe.apps.mil/. Phase I submissions must be received by the Government via encrypted DoD SAFE submission no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 20, 2026 . GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT: Agreements Officer - Ms. Caryl Williams - caryl.a.williams.civ@us.navy.mil Agreements Specialist - Ms. Jada Williams - jada.n.williams11.civ@us.navy.mil Agreements Specialist - Ms. Alaina Fletcher - alaina.s.fletcher.civ@us.navy.mil NOTE: For Companies invited to participate in Phase II only, the Government will distribute CLASSIFIED TLRD Annex(es) to Companies eligible to receive CLASSIFIED data and may elect to release additional information. HARD COPIES OF MAILED OR HAND DELIVERED WHITE PAPERS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. Submissions sent through other channels not identified in this Notice, or after the Phase I White Paper submission deadline, will not be reviewed nor evaluated by the Government. DEADLINES: Q&A : by 6:00 p.m. ET on October 2, 2026 DoD SAFE Link Request : by 6:00 p.m. on October 13, 2026 Phase I Submission : by 6

events.text: SAM.gov solicitation 2026-09-22: AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation (RFP or RFQ); solicitation N0002426R6222; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/fd41d107a67b49f7b37a10bbbc058a2b?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 e9f2a1a36878 Description NOTE: On 22 September 2026, Solicitation Amendment 002 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L and other changes, all of which are identified in the Amendment summary of changes. The solicitation also extends the proposal due date to 5 November 2026 at 4:00 pm Eastern Standard Time. NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy's Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company's DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. outcomes.text: SAM.gov solicitation 2023-11-02: Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence Training Virtual E solicitation (RFP or RFQ); solicitation N00039-23-R-9002; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/7152df629ca84e939b603f309d487362?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-22 sha256 1c9c9f0236c7 02 NOV 2023: Amendment 04 and Q&A Set 03 are posted ***** 30 OCT 2023: Amendment 03 and Q&A Set 02 are posted. ***** 16 OCT 2023: Amendment 02 and Q&A Set 01 are posted. ***** 28 SEP 2023: Amendment 01 is posted. ***** 26 SEP 2023: The Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR), in support of the Program Executive Office for Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (PEO C4I) Program Manager, Warfare (PMW) 160, Tactical Networks, has issued a Full and Open competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) N00039-23-R-9002 for the procurement of the C4I Training Virtual Environment (C4I TVE) requirement. ***** This synopsis serves to meet the requirement of FAR 5.201. The Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR), in support of the Program Executive Office for Command Control, Communications and Computers (PEO C4I) Program Manager, Warfare (PMW) 160, Tactical Networks, intends to issue a Full and Open competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) N00039-23-R-9002 for the procurement of a Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence Training Virtual Environment (C4I TVE) Contract. The RFP will be released in Q4FY23, with a contract award estimated for the Q3FY24 timeframe. The Department of the Navy (DoN) requires continued operations, maintenance, and sustainment of the Training Virtual Environment (TVE) capability that supports Consolidated Afloat Network Enterprise Services (CANES) system administration training, other emergent training, and performance support requirements in support of Fleet readiness. The TVE is a proctored, web-based, cloud- hosted learning solution that provides Information Technology (IT) administration, management, and troubleshooting of the CANES capability in a virtualized environment that fully replicates the functionality of all CANES variants fielded in the Fleet. The TVE architecture leverages commercial and Federal cloud best practices to enable scalability and flexibility of operations for CANES Administrator training to include hosted and/or connected Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) applications. The C4I TVE (formally referred to as the CANES TVE) procurement will be conducted under full and open competition. The Government anticipates issuing a single-award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. The contract will include a five (5) year ordering period. The Government anticipates utilizing a Cost Plus Fixed Price (CPFF) CLIN structure for C4I TVE Engineering Services and a Cost CLIN for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). This notice is provided for information only; it is not a Request for Proposal and is not be to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a contract. The Government will not pay for any effort expended in response to this notice. Any information submitted in response to the synopsis will become property of the U.S. Government. All questions/comments concerning this synopsis are to be submitted in writing to Contract Specialist, Jennifer Zornow, email address at Jennifer.L.Zornow.civ@us.navy.mil and Contracting Officer, Susana Wiker, email address at Susana L.Wiker.civ@us.navy.mil. Future information, if released, will be synopsized on the System for Award Management at https://www.sam.gov/ and NAVWAR E-Commerce Central website at https://www.e- commerce.dc3n.navy.mil. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring these sites for additional information pertaining to this notice.

outcomes.text: SAM.gov presolicitation 2024-06-06: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for Field Service Representativ presolicitation (intent to solicit); solicitation N00039-24-Q-5001; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/70eed15b18e84c8799bfc2b072edee4b?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-22 sha256 b3c2281a6902 The RFQ number has changed to N00039-24-Q-2000. ********************************************************************* The purpose of this notice is to inform all parties that the United States Navy, Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAWARSYSCOM) in support of the Program Executive Office for Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (PEO C4I) (PMW 790) intends to award a sole source follow- on contract for Field Service Representative (FSR) on its Portable Radios to Harris Corporation, RF Communications Division (Harris), located at 1680 University Ave., Rochester, NY 14610. Harris is the current OEM vendor providing PRP radios and ancillary parts. As the developer, sole maintainer, and owner of all data rights of the radios, L3Harris has unique and detailed knowledge of its radio's requirements and training. Therefore, all subcontractors must have certified training by L3Harris in order to maintain and train on the L3Harris' radios. L3Harris remains the only qualified source for the training and maintenance of its radios. Because of its expertise and proprietary waveforms, L3Harris is the only vendor currently possessing the capability to immediately train and maintain the radios to ensure uninterrupted service. The FSR shall serve as in-house subject matter expert (SME) on the disassembly, testing, maintenance, and assembly of the core L3Harris Communication Systems product lines. The FSR shall coordinate, support, and conduct technical activities (involving L3Harris Technologies, Inc., Harris Defense Communications products and systems). This effort will cover continued services for 12 months base with three 12-month option years. This announcement is for subcontracting possibilities only. The NAICS for this procurement is 611430 (with a Small Business Size Standard of $15M). There will be no written solicitation issued. This is an intent to purchase a sole source procurement under the authority of FAR 6.302-1. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals nor a solicitation of offers. Responses to this notice should be directed to Heidi Radaford at heidi.l.radaford.civ@us.navy.mil or Steffany Becker at steffany.a.becker.civ@us.navy.mil. This notice is also posted on the NAVWAR e-commerce website at https://e-commerce.sscno.nmci.navy.mil. Sole Source authority FAR Subpart 6.302-1 will satisfy the agency requirements. IMPORTANT NOTES: Information submitted will not be returned to the respective respondents. Oral submissions of information are not acceptable and will not be accepted in response to this notice.

outcomes.text: SAM.gov presolicitation 2024-08-23: PEO MLB Small Business Industry Day presolicitation (intent to solicit); solicitation N00039-24-R-4025; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/60d9c953f94341fa8e8b4a2ede47564c?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-22 sha256 1efb446dfc93 On Wednesday, Oct. 30, from 9:30 am EST - 4:35 pm EST, the Naval Information Warfare Systems Command's (NAVWAR) Program Executive Office for Manpower, Logistics, and Business Solutions (PEO MLB) will host a Small Business Industry Day at the National Museum of the United States Army, 1775 Liberty Drive, Ft. Belvoir, VA. We are excited to extend this opportunity to meet face-to-face with PEO MLB leadership. PEO MLB attendees will include our program and portfolio managers. PEO MLB collaborates with our customers and stakeholders to acquire creative and innovative solutions that address the complex challenges of operating a globally distributed workforce. Our portfolio of programs delivers a broad range of defense business IT solutions that provide the foundational systems and processes to man, train and equip the Sailors, Marines, and the civilian workforce of the United States Navy and United States Marine Corps around the world. The Small Business Industry Day will kick off with a welcome from PEO MLB Program Executive Officer, Ms. Christine Rodriguez, and PEO MLB Executive Director, Ms. Mary Thoms. We will also hear from distinguished guest speaker, Office of Small Business Planning, Deputy Director, Ms. Arveice Washington. PEO MLB's Program Managers (PM)/Deputy Program Managers (DPM) will give presentations providing an overview of capabilities, challenges, and growth areas within their respective programs. Following these briefs, we are holding an exhibit hall style Industry Fair allowing industry representatives to meet with MLB program leadership to discuss potential collaboration. Space is limited! Two guests per company may attend in person, with attendance capped at 160 on-site guests. A virtual watch/view only option for the event is available for those who are unable to attend in person. Attendance is limited at 400 participants for the virtual option. Our event will host 160 guests in person and up to 400 separately on a virtual stream; those watching will view the presenters and briefings upon completion of that portion the stream will end. Please note that Industry Fair (meet and greet) will only be conducted in person and will not be offered virtually. More information to follow this post! For question regarding this event, please email PEO_MLB_Small_Business@us.navy.mil.

Questions/comments on the DRAFT RFP are to be submitted NLT 2:00 pm Eastern Time on 20 August 2024. Not all DRAFT RFP Section J attachments are posted at this time; the remaining attachments will be posted with the final RFP. The DRAFT RFP is posted for informational purposes only. ****Revised Draft CDRL Documents posting for 4Jun24*** This posting updates the CDRL files Att 2 and L-7 with revised embedded Staffing enclosures to provide easier access. These updated documents are provided for comment to be submitted NLT 2:00 pm Eastern Time on 11 June 2024. ****Revised Draft CDRL Documents posting for 31May24*** This posting updates the CDRL files Att 2 and L-7 with revised embedded CDAD enclosures to provide easier access. These updated documents are provided for comment to be submitted NLT 2:00 pm Eastern Time on 11 June 2024. ****Pre-solicitation posting for 28May24*** Pre-solicitation Notice for Personnel and Pay Integration and Sustainment The Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR), on behalf of MyNavy Human Resources (HR) Information Technology (IT) Solutions (PMW 240), Program Executive Office Manpower, Logistics & Business Solutions (PEO MLB), is issuing this pre-solicitation notice for PMW 240's Personnel & Pay Integration and Sustainment requirement. PMW 240 is responsible for the acquisition and sustainment of the Navy's manpower, personnel, training and education systems and the transformation of the Navy's HR systems. The Navy Standard Integrated Personnel System (NSIPS) is the Navy's current operational IT system providing the Navy's HR personnel capabilities. This effort is for the continued NSIPS operation, sustainment, and integration with pay capabilities (Navy Personnel and Pay (NP2)). This effort includes system integration, testing, implementation, operation, and sustainment of NSIPS capabilities that are currently being performed by GDIT, under contract N00039-23-C-0002. NSIPS sustainment includes deployment and production support, application maintenance, environmental maintenance, legacy system integration, afloat installation maintenance, and interface development and maintenance centered on the existing PeopleSoft-based capabilities. This effort includes personnel and pay systems integration, hosting, operations, cybersecurity support, and operation of a service desk. A key part of this effort is maintenance and operation of the cloud-based environments hosting HR capabilities and compliance with all applicable DoD Information Assurance/Cyber Security rules and regulations. NAVWAR intends to issue a full and open competition Request for Proposal (RFP) that is anticipated to result in the award of a single-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (ID/IQ) contract, with an initial Task Order at contract award, utilizing the procedures in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 15. The new contract will have an ordering period of at least five years and the initial Task Order will have a five-year period of performance that includes a twelve-month base period and four twelve-month options. Award is anticipated in the March 2024 timeframe with a total ordering ceiling of $338M. The Government anticipates using the attached requirements documents (Attachments 1 and 2; and L-6 and L-7, respectively) to define the tasking. Industry feedback on the attached PWS and CDRLs is important in meeting the Government's requirement. Please use the attached Comment Response Form, Attachment L-1, to comment on the PWS and CDRLs. Questions concerning the attached PWS' and CDRLs' shall be provided via e-mail to the following: Gina Boyanton, Contract Specialist, virginia.s.boyanton.civ@us.navy.mil Shaan Charran, Contract Specialist, shaan.a.charran.civ@us.navy.mil Rachel Locke, Contract Specialist, Rachel.a.locke3.civ@us.navy.mil Matthew Edson, Contracting Officer, at matthew.j.edson.civ@us.navy.mil Responses are due NLT 2:00 pm Eastern Time on 11 June 2024. Product Service Code: DA01 IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Support Services (Labor) NAICS Code: 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services A Draft RFP is anticipated. The tentative timeline for the solicitation and award is as follows: RFP release:1 July 2024 Proposal Submission date:1 August 2024 Anticipated Award date:15 March 2025 THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR A SOLICITATION OF OFFERS.
