outcomes.text: SAM.gov solicitation 2026-09-22: AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation (RFP or RFQ); solicitation N0002426R6222; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/fd41d107a67b49f7b37a10bbbc058a2b?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 e9f2a1a36878 Description NOTE: On 22 September 2026, Solicitation Amendment 002 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L and other changes, all of which are identified in the Amendment summary of changes. The solicitation also extends the proposal due date to 5 November 2026 at 4:00 pm Eastern Standard Time. NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy's Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company's DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. outcomes.text: SAM.gov solicitation 2026-09-22: Low Profile Mast and Rotational Module Component Prototype Other Transaction Are area of interest under a commercial solutions opening (solicitation); solicitation N00024-26-R-6215; record https://sam.gov/api/prod/opps/v2/opportunities/47e1c5d28e634633bcdf0820327d6a3c?api_key=null retrieved 2026-09-23 sha256 23125fbac152 Team Submarines, Australia, United Kingdom, and United States (AUKUS), International & Systems (AI&S), Submarine Electromagnetic Systems Program Office (PMS 435) is pleased to release a competitive Area of Interest (AOI) announcement for the Low Profile Mast (LPM) and Rotational Module (RM) component to address several key operational needs. The LPM/RM programs seek innovative technologies that accelerate the prototyping of capabilities that address these key operational needs. To accelerate the design, development and demonstration of LPM/RM capabilities, the Navy will be utilizing the Other Transaction Authority pathway outlined in Title 10 U.S.C. § 4022. It is intended that this solicitation may result in the award of one or more prototype projects. There are nine (9) attachments to this AOI, some of which contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): LPM/RM Terms of Use Agreement AOI AOI Guidance CUI LPM Type 24 Mod 1Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI LPM Verification Guide (VG) [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Verification Guide [RESTRICTED] LPM/RM AOI Questions Form CUI LPM/RM Placemat Template [RESTRICTED] Companies are advised to proceed with the following steps to respond to this notice: STEP 1 - Terms of Use Agreement (TOU) Several key documents related to the LPM Type 24 Mod 1 and RM are only releasable to eligible businesses with ownership in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Non-Australia, United Kingdom, or United States foreign-owned businesses may submit a technical solution as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more Australia, United Kingdom, or United States-owned businesses. The ability to be awarded an Agreement may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain access to restricted information. Companies interested in submitting a technical solution in response to the AOI shall complete Attachment 1: TOU Agreement and return it via e-mail to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialists listed in this notice. The Company point of contact that will request access to the restricted documents in this notice shall be the Company point of contact listed in the TOU. Companies should also request access to the restricted CUI documents in SAM at the time of TOU submittal to the Government. Once the signed TOU is received and verified, Team Submarines will grant access to the restricted CUI documents and transmit relevant UNCLASSIFIED Government-Furnished Information (GFI) relevant to the AOI to the Company point of contact listed in the TOU. NOTE: The TOU provided as Attachment 1 is specific to this AOI release; if a Company previously submitted a TOU under prior LPM/RM Industry Day notice, that Company must submit a separate TOU for this AOI opportunity. STEP 2 - QUESTIONS & ANSWERS OPPORTUNITY Companies may submit questions using Attachment 8: LPM/RM AOI Questions Form. Team Submarine will only accept Q&A submissions up to the CUI level. Q&A submissions shall be submitted electronically via e-mail to the Government points of contact listed in this notice no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 2, 2026 . -SUBJECT: N00024-26-R-6215 Q&A This opportunity is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or for the information provided in response to this notice. The Government may or may not respond to Q&A submissions and reserves the right to redact the content of submissions prior to any release back to industry. The Government may use the information and feedback provided in Q&A submissions to inform future solicitations as necessary. Respondents are solely responsible for properly marking and clearly identifying any proprietary information or trade secrets contained in any submission in response to this notice. Opting not to submit any Q&A does not preclude participation in this AOI or any future engagements. It is the responsibility of industry to monitor the Government Point of Entry (GPE) for official AOI communications. STEP 4 - Companies shall submit Phase I White Papers and Placemats electronically via encrypted DoD SAFE transmission. Companies must request a DoD SAFE link by e-mailing ALL Government points contract listed in this notice no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 13, 2026. -SUBJECT: [insert LPM or RM] N00024-26-R-6215 DoD SAFE Link [insert COMPANY NAME] If a Company intends to send a Phase I submission for both LPM and RM, that Company must request two separate DoD SAFE links. Companies are encouraged to submit White Papers prior to the latest closing date. Inclusion of a delivery receipt with an email submission will be the only indication of the Government's successful receipt of a White Paper. Each Company must comply with DoD SAFE file size limitations and other guidance as provided at https://safe.apps.mil/. Phase I submissions must be received by the Government via encrypted DoD SAFE submission no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 20, 2026 . GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT: Agreements Officer - Ms. Caryl Williams - caryl.a.williams.civ@us.navy.mil Agreements Specialist - Ms. Jada Williams - jada.n.williams11.civ@us.navy.mil Agreements Specialist - Ms. Alaina Fletcher - alaina.s.fletcher.civ@us.navy.mil NOTE: For Companies invited to participate in Phase II only, the Government will distribute CLASSIFIED TLRD Annex(es) to Companies eligible to receive CLASSIFIED data and may elect to release additional information.
